Source hashes, historical-to-accepted upstream locator resolution, chapter ranges and document statistics. This is provenance metadata, not mathematical assertions or proof evidence.

Historical source map, dependency routing, group labels, proof-route descriptions, source hashes, version pins and document statistics. These are advisory metadata; they neither add proof-internal steps to the required results nor establish any candidate theorem.

For the connected finite bipartite graph walk, point-start laws alternate the two parts; its cyclic subsequence limits and Cesaro limits are the W17 specialization. The agreed w24_graph_period_mixing goal specifies half stationary mass per part, limits twice pi restricted to the corresponding part, and Cesaro TV convergence from arbitrary initial law.

For the neighbor walk on a finite connected bipartite simple graph with at least two vertices, point-start laws alternate bipartition parts. The cyclic residue laws converge in total variation to twice the degree stationary law restricted to the corresponding part, and Cesàro laws converge to the degree stationary law. Each part has stationary mass one half.

For the bipartite finite connected graph walk, laws from a single vertex alternate its two parts; the cyclic even/odd subsequences converge in total variation to twice the degree stationary law restricted to the appropriate part, and Cesàro laws converge to the stationary law. Each part has stationary mass one half.
Title, document layout, references, and overview of the two parts and nine chapters. These are exposition and scope information, not additional mathematical obligations.
The spectrum of the zero ring is empty.

All rings are commutative with identity and all ring maps preserve identity; the zero ring is allowed. Algebra towers have compatible structural maps, and tensor products use the indicated scalar structures. Notation: Spec(B), B_q and κ(q) denote the prime spectrum, prime localization and residue field; B_b is localization at powers of b, and base change along A→A′ is B′=A′⊗_A B. These conventions govern the obligations throughout the paper.
An A-algebra is a commutative unital ring B equipped with a specified unital structural map A→B; in a tower of algebras the structural maps are compatible.
An A-algebra B is essentially of finite type over A if B is a localization of an A-algebra of finite type.
An A-algebra is of finite type if it admits a finite set of A-algebra generators.
A finitely presented A-algebra is a quotient A[X₁,…,X_n]/I for some finite n and some finitely generated ideal I.
A finitely presented module is the cokernel of a linear map between finite free modules. Finiteness of an algebra as a module is distinguished from finite type as an algebra.

P1-03 and D07 provide previously developed algebra and field theory; the source map records references, dependencies and candidate interfaces. Geometric regularity, differential sheaves, the full cotangent complex, local cohomology and dualizing complexes, finite flat refinements of étale covers, and étale-local lifting of coprime factorizations are assigned to other treatments and create no extra obligation here.

Chapter 1 introduces Kähler differentials as first-order variation and explains that coefficient-module scalar structures distinguish transitivity, conormal, and base-change statements. Throughout this chapter A→B is a unital homomorphism of commutative rings, M is a B-module, the zero ring is permitted, and compatible towers use the induced scalar actions. The cited earlier notes supply quotient, tensor, scalar-extension/restriction, and tensor-right-exactness preliminaries; these citations and motivation are context, not extra results.

For a unital map A→B of commutative rings and a B-module M, an A-derivation D:B→M is an A-linear map satisfying D(bb′)=bD(b′)+b′D(b) for every b,b′∈B. Equivalently, it is an additive map satisfying this rule and vanishing on the image of A. Such maps form the B-module Der_A(B,M) with pointwise operations. Composition with a B-linear M→N gives a map of derivation modules. Two A-derivations B→M that agree on an A-algebra generating family of B are equal.

For every unital A→B there is a B-module Ω_{B/A} and an A-derivation d_{B/A}:B→Ω_{B/A} such that, for every B-module M, composition with d gives a B-linear isomorphism Hom_B(Ω_{B/A},M)≅Der_A(B,M), natural in M. Construct Ω as the free B-module on symbols [b] for b∈B modulo the submodule generated by [b+b′]−[b]−[b′], [bb′]−b[b′]−b′[b], and [a_B] for a∈A. Put db equal to the class of [b]; these db generate Ω. The universal property determines the pair up to its unique isomorphism respecting the derivation.
For T=B⊗_A B, multiplication μ:T→B, and J=ker μ, the B-actions induced by the two tensor factors agree on J/J². There is a B-linear isomorphism Ω_{B/A}≅J/J² sending every db to the class of 1⊗b−b⊗1.

For a B-module M, make B⊕M a ring by componentwise addition, identity (1,0), and (b,m)(b′,m′)=(bb′,bm′+b′m), and give it its A-algebra structure by A→B→B⊕M with b↦(b,0). The A-algebra sections of its projection to B are exactly b↦(b,D(b)) as D ranges over Der_A(B,M).

Let C be an A-algebra, I⊆C an ideal with I²=0, and f̄:B→C/I an A-algebra map. Multiplication by any lifts of scalars defines a well-defined C/I-module structure on I. Regard I as a B-module through f̄. If f:B→C is an A-algebra lift of f̄, every A-algebra lift of f̄ is uniquely f+D for D∈Der_A(B,I), and every such f+D is a lift.

Every commutative square of unital ring maps (A→B)→(A′→B′), whose target map is f:B→B′, induces a natural B-linear map Ω_{B/A}→Ω_{B′/A′}, with the target restricted along f, sending db↦d(f(b)). These maps respect identity squares and composition of squares.
If A→B is surjective then Ω_{B/A}=0. In particular Ω_{A/A}=0 and Ω_{(A/I)/A}=0 for every ideal I⊆A.

For any set Λ and polynomial A-algebra P=A[X_i:i∈Λ], the elements dX_i form a free P-basis of Ω_{P/A}. For every f∈P, df=∑_{i∈Λ}(∂f/∂X_i)dX_i, where the sum has finite support. For P=A[X] this reads df=f′(X)dX.
For every compatible tower A→B→C there are canonical C-linear maps u:C⊗_B Ω_{B/A}→Ω_{C/A} and v:Ω_{C/A}→Ω_{C/B}, characterized by u(c⊗db)=c d_{C/A}(b_C) and v(d_{C/A}c)=d_{C/B}c.

For every compatible tower A→B→C and the canonical maps u(c⊗db)=c d_{C/A}(b_C), v(d_{C/A}c)=d_{C/B}c, the sequence C⊗_B Ω_{B/A}→Ω_{C/A}→Ω_{C/B}→0 is exact: v is surjective and im u=ker v. There exist such towers of commutative unital rings for which the first map has nonzero kernel; no injectivity assertion is part of this exact sequence.

In any commutative square (A→B)→(A′→B′) with f:B→B′ surjective, the induced B-linear map Ω_{B/A}→Ω_{B′/A′} is surjective. Its kernel is the B-submodule generated by all db for b∈B such that f(b) belongs to im(A′→B′).

For any compatible A→P↠B with I=ker(P→B), the formula j([f])=1⊗df defines a B-linear map I/I²→B⊗_P Ω_{P/A}. With the canonical map to Ω_{B/A}, the sequence I/I²→B⊗_P Ω_{P/A}→Ω_{B/A}→0 is exact at its middle and last terms. There exist such towers of commutative unital rings for which the first map has nonzero kernel; injectivity at I/I² is not asserted.

For any finite presentation B=A[X_1,…,X_n]/(f_1,…,f_m), Ω_{B/A} is the cokernel of the B-linear map B^m→B^n given by e_j↦∑_{i=1}^n overline(∂f_j/∂X_i)e_i. The i-th vector in B^n maps to d X̄_i. Thus this Jacobian matrix has rows indexed by variables and columns indexed by relations, including the cases of zero variables or zero relations.
If B is of finite type as an A-algebra, then Ω_{B/A} is finitely generated as a B-module. If B is finitely presented as an A-algebra, then Ω_{B/A} is finitely presented as a B-module.

For a compatible tower A→P↠B where P→B has kernel I and an A-algebra section s:B→P, its conormal sequence 0→I/I²→B⊗_P Ω_{P/A}→Ω_{B/A}→0 is split short exact. A left inverse of j([f])=1⊗df is the B-linear map corresponding to the A-derivation P→I/I², p↦[p−s(p̄)].
For an ideal I⊆B, an integer n≥1, and B_i=B/I^i, the map induced on differentials gives an isomorphism of B_n-modules B_n⊗_B Ω_{B/A}≅B_n⊗_{B_{n+1}} Ω_{B_{n+1}/A}.

For a field k, B=k[t], I=(t), and n=1, both B_1⊗_B Ω_{B/k} and B_1⊗_{B_2} Ω_{B_2/k} are k dt, whereas Ω_{B_1/k}=Ω_{k/k}=0. This illustrates that restricting the differentials of a thicker quotient differs from taking the differentials of the reduced quotient.

Let S be any multiplicative subset of B and T=S⁻¹B, with no exclusion of 0∈S or zero divisors. For every T-module N, every A-derivation D:B→N extends uniquely to an A-derivation D̃:T→N, with D̃(b/s)=s⁻¹D(b)−bs⁻²D(s). Consequently S⁻¹Ω_{B/A}≅Ω_{T/A}, sending db/1↦d(b/1). If U⊆A is multiplicative and its image is invertible in B, the natural base-change map Ω_{B/A}→Ω_{B/U⁻¹A} is an isomorphism.

For every ring map A→A′ and B′=A′⊗_A B, with no flatness hypothesis, there is a canonical B′-linear isomorphism B′⊗_B Ω_{B/A}≅Ω_{B′/A′} taking b′⊗db↦b′ d(1⊗b). The isomorphisms are compatible with identity base change and composition of base changes under the canonical tensor associativity isomorphisms.

For A-algebras B_1 and B_2 and C=B_1⊗_A B_2, there is a canonical C-linear isomorphism Ω_{C/A}≅(C⊗_{B_1}Ω_{B_1/A})⊕(C⊗_{B_2}Ω_{B_2/A}), sending d(b_1⊗b_2) to (b_2(1⊗db_1), b_1(1⊗db_2)), with both coefficients mapped to C. In particular for C=B_1[X_i:i∈Λ], the second summand is ⊕_{i∈Λ} C dX_i.

For a system of ring maps (A_i→B_i) indexed by any nonempty directed set and compatible transition squares, let A=colim_i A_i and B=colim_i B_i. The transition maps induce a B-linear isomorphism colim_i(B⊗_{B_i}Ω_{B_i/A_i})≅Ω_{B/A}.

For two A-algebra maps u,v:P⇉Q and their coequalizer C in A-algebras, Ω_{C/A} is naturally the cokernel of the difference between the two induced C-linear maps C⊗_P Ω_{P/A}⇉C⊗_Q Ω_{Q/A}. The P-action on C is the common composite through u and v.

For any finite family (B_i) of A-algebras and B=∏_i B_i, the coordinate projections induce a B-linear isomorphism Ω_{B/A}≅∏_i Ω_{B_i/A}, with scalar action on each factor via its projection. This includes the empty family: B is the zero ring and its differential module is zero.

Let P=A[X_1,…,X_n] and B=P/(f). The B-module Ω_{B/A} is generated by d X̄_i with the single defining relation ∑_i overline(∂_i f)d X̄_i=0. In one variable Ω_{B/A}≅B/(f′(X̄)) d X̄. For k[x,y]/(xy) the relation is y dx+x dy=0. For k[ε]/(ε²) the relation is 2ε dε=0. If k is a field of characteristic 2, the latter differential module is free of rank 1 and ε is a nonzero nilpotent element of the algebra.
For a field k of characteristic different from 2, the differential module of k[ε]/(ε²) over k is the copy of k dε on which ε acts by zero.

For a finite simple algebraic field extension L=K[α] with minimal polynomial f, Ω_{L/K}≅L/(f′(α)) dα. In particular it vanishes when L/K is separable. If char K=p>0 and X^p−a is irreducible over K, adjoining a root gives an extension whose module of relative differentials has dimension 1 over that extension field.

For every separable algebraic field extension L/K, finite or infinite, and every ring map A→K, the canonical map L⊗_K Ω_{K/A}→Ω_{L/A} is an isomorphism. In particular Ω_{L/K}=0 for every separable algebraic extension, including infinite ones.

For an A-algebra point x:B→K to a field K, the K-linear dual of K⊗_B Ω_{B/A} is naturally Der_A(B,K), where the B-action on K is given by x. Equivalently this is the vector space of A-algebra lifts of x to K[ε]/(ε²), with the constant lift through K as its zero; the derivation D corresponds to b↦x(b)+εD(b).
When A=K=k is a field and x:B→k is a k-algebra point with m=ker x, there is a canonical k-linear isomorphism m/m²≅k⊗_B Ω_{B/k} sending [b]↦1⊗db for b∈m.

For q∈Spec B, p=q∩A, A′=κ(p), B′=A′⊗_A B, and K=κ(q), there is a natural A′-algebra map B′→K and a canonical isomorphism K⊗_B Ω_{B/A}≅K⊗_{B′}Ω_{B′/A′}. On the left one can equivalently use K⊗_{B_q}Ω_{B_q/A_p}; these identifications are canonical and compatible with the point and the maps on differential generators.

For every f∈A, Ω_{A_f/A}=0. For every field K, Ω_{K(t)/K} is free on dt. For every prime integer p, Ω_{𝔽_p/ℤ}=0 although ℤ→𝔽_p is not flat: multiplication by p is injective on ℤ and becomes the zero endomorphism of the nonzero module 𝔽_p after tensoring.

The chapter closes by interpreting the three already stated ring-change examples and announcing that the nonflat quotient will be used to compare infinitesimal uniqueness and existence. It introduces no additional mathematical obligation.

Chapter 2 motivates square-zero lifting as first-order lifting with separate existence and uniqueness issues and explains the roles of differentials and polynomial equations. The Stacks and Hartshorne citations provide source context; no extra theorem is imposed by these references.

For a unital ring map A→B, and for every A-algebra C and ideal N⊆C with N²=0, consider the reduction map Hom_{A-alg}(B,C)→Hom_{A-alg}(B,C/N). The map A→B is formally smooth if all these maps are surjective, formally unramified if all are injective, and formally étale if all are bijective. There is no finite-generation or finite-presentation assumption.

Each of formal smoothness, formal unramifiedness, and formal étaleness is equivalent to its defining reduction-map condition with N allowed to be any nilpotent ideal, in every test A-algebra C, instead of only square-zero ideals.

Let N²=0 in an A-algebra C, let u:B→C/N be an A-algebra map, and regard N as a B-module via u and multiplication by lifted scalars. If u has an A-algebra lift v:B→C, then h↦v+h d_{B/A} is a bijection Hom_B(Ω_{B/A},N)→{A-algebra lifts of u}. Replacing v by v+h_0d changes the coordinate h to h−h_0. Thus the additive group Hom_B(Ω_{B/A},N) acts freely and transitively on every nonempty fiber of the reduction map.
For every A-algebra B, with no finiteness hypotheses, A→B is formally unramified if and only if Ω_{B/A}=0.

For any indexing set Λ, the polynomial algebra A[X_λ:λ∈Λ] is formally smooth over A. More strongly, every A-algebra map from this polynomial algebra to the target of any surjective A-algebra homomorphism lifts to its source.

Let P↠B be a surjective A-algebra map with kernel I, and suppose P is formally smooth over A. Put L=I/I² and F=B⊗_P Ω_{P/A}, with conormal map δ:L→F. Given a square-zero ideal N⊆C in an A-algebra C and a map u:B→C/N, choose an A-algebra lift φ:P→C of P→B→C/N. Then o_φ:L→N, [f]↦φ(f), is B-linear, with N acted on through u. Its class in coker(Hom_B(F,N)→Hom_B(L,N)), where the map sends h to h∘δ, is independent of φ and is zero if and only if u has an A-algebra lift to C.

For a finite polynomial presentation B=A[X_1,…,X_n]/(f_1,…,f_m), a square-zero ideal N⊆C, an A-algebra map u:B→C/N, and representatives x_i∈C of u(X̄_i), replacing x_i by x_i+t_i for t_i∈N changes each equation value f_j(x_1,…,x_n) by ∑_i u(overline(∂_i f_j))t_i, acting on N through C/N. Hence such corrected representatives define a lift of u precisely when they solve ∑_i u(overline(∂_i f_j))t_i=−f_j(x_1,…,x_n) in N for every j.

Let P↠B be a surjective A-algebra map with kernel I and P formally smooth over A. The following are equivalent: B is formally smooth over A; P/I²→B has an A-algebra section; the conormal sequence 0→I/I²→B⊗_P Ω_{P/A}→Ω_{B/A}→0 is split exact as a sequence of B-modules, with the first map [f]↦1⊗df.

For any polynomial A-algebra presentation P↠B with kernel I and conormal map δ:I/I²→B⊗_P Ω_{P/A}, B is formally smooth over A if and only if δ is injective and Ω_{B/A} is projective over B. If so, I/I² and Ω_{B/A} are direct summands of the free B-module B⊗_P Ω_{P/A}. When B is finitely presented over A and the polynomial presentation is finite, both summands are finite projective B-modules.
Formal smoothness, formal unramifiedness, and formal étaleness are each preserved by composition of compatible ring maps and by arbitrary base change A→A′ with new algebra A′⊗_A B.

For every compatible tower A→B→D, if A→B is formally unramified and A→D is formally smooth, then B→D is formally smooth. If A→D is formally unramified, then B→D is formally unramified, without any condition on A→B.

For any multiplicative set S⊆B, the localization B→S⁻¹B is formally étale, including the case 0∈S. For each of formal smoothness, formal unramifiedness, and formal étaleness, localizing the target preserves the property. If U⊆A is a multiplicative set whose image consists of units in B, the property for A→B is equivalent to that for the induced U⁻¹A→B.

Suppose B is finitely presented over A and b_1,…,b_s generate the unit ideal of B. For each formal property (smooth, unramified, or étale), the property for every A→B_{b_i} implies it for A→B; the converse follows from localization preservation. For formal unramifiedness no finite-presentation assumption is required, and A→B is formally unramified if and only if A→B_q is formally unramified for every q∈Spec B. The finite cover may be empty when B is the zero ring.
For any unital ring map A→B, formal étaleness is equivalent to formal smoothness together with Ω_{B/A}=0.
For a compatible tower A→B→D with B→D formally étale, the canonical D-linear map D⊗_B Ω_{B/A}→Ω_{D/A}, 1⊗db↦d(b_D), is an isomorphism.
For every ideal I⊆A, the quotient map A→A/I is formally unramified. It is formally smooth if and only if it is formally étale if and only if I=I².
For a field k of characteristic p>0, the k-algebra B=k[X]/(X^p) has a free B-module of differentials Ω_{B/k} of rank 1, but it is not formally smooth over k.
For every compatible tower A→B→D with B→D formally smooth, the canonical transitivity sequence 0→D⊗_B Ω_{B/A}→Ω_{D/A}→Ω_{D/B}→0 is split exact as a sequence of D-modules.

Let A→B be formally étale, let J⊆B be an ideal such that A→B/J is surjective, and let I=ker(A→B/J). For every integer n≥1 the canonical map A/I^n→B/J^n is an isomorphism. These canonical maps induce an isomorphism of associated graded rings ⊕_{n≥0} I^n/I^{n+1}≅⊕_{n≥0} J^n/J^{n+1}, including degree zero.

For a compatible tower A→B→D with B→D formally étale, put J_B=ker(B⊗_A B→B) and J_D=ker(D⊗_A D→D), where the maps are multiplication. For every integer n≥0, the natural map D⊗_B((B⊗_A B)/J_B^{n+1})→(D⊗_A D)/J_D^{n+1}, extending scalars using the first copy of B, is an isomorphism. For n=1, its induced map on the square-zero diagonal ideals agrees, under their identifications with differentials, with D⊗_B Ω_{B/A}≅Ω_{D/A}.
A filtered colimit of formally étale A-algebras is formally étale over A. A filtered colimit of formally unramified A-algebras is formally unramified over A.

Let A′ be faithfully flat over A and B′=A′⊗_A B. If A′→B′ is formally unramified, then A→B is formally unramified, with no finite-presentation hypothesis. If B is finitely presented over A, formal smoothness and formal étaleness also descend from A′→B′ to A→B.

For a finitely presented formally smooth A-algebra B, every A-algebra map B→C/N lifts to C whenever C is an A-algebra and N⊆C is a nil ideal (each element is nilpotent), without requiring N itself to be nilpotent. For a finite-type formally unramified A-algebra B, any two A-algebra maps B→C that agree modulo such a nil ideal are equal. Consequently finitely presented formally étale A-algebras have both existence and uniqueness for nil-ideal tests.

The transition to Chapter 3 announces adding finite presentation to formal smoothness and studying the resulting finite conormal data by Jacobian matrices on principal opens. It adds no separate mathematical assertion beyond the definitions and results that follow.

Chapter 3 assumes a commutative base ring A and explains that finite presentation turns the unrestricted formal lifting criterion into local finite Jacobian calculations. This is motivation and context.

An A-algebra B is smooth if it is finitely presented over A and formally smooth over A. Here finite presentation means the existence of an A-algebra presentation B≅A[X_1,…,X_n]/(f_1,…,f_c) with finite n and c, and formal smoothness requires existence of lifts for every test A-algebra and every square-zero ideal.

Suppose B is finitely presented over A and P=A[X_1,…,X_n]↠B has kernel I. Then B is smooth over A if and only if d_I:I/I²→B⊗_P Ω_{P/A}, [f]↦1⊗df, admits a B-linear left inverse. If so, 0→I/I²→B⊗_P Ω_{P/A}→Ω_{B/A}→0 is split exact and I/I² and Ω_{B/A} are finite projective B-modules. Equivalently, smoothness holds if and only if d_I is injective and Ω_{B/A} is projective. The criterion applies to every finite polynomial presentation of B.

A finite presentation B=A[X_1,…,X_n]/(f_1,…,f_c), with 0≤c≤n, is standard smooth if a c×c minor of the Jacobian matrix (∂f_j/∂X_i)_{1≤i≤n,1≤j≤c}, using all c columns, has unit image in B. After reordering variables its rows can be taken as 1,…,c. For c=0 the minor determinant is 1. An A-algebra is standard smooth if it admits such a presentation.

An A-algebra B given by a standard smooth presentation A[X_1,…,X_n]/(f_1,…,f_c) is smooth over A. After ordering variables so the unit minor uses rows 1,…,c, the conormal module I/I² has B-basis [f_1],…,[f_c], and Ω_{B/A} has B-basis d X̄_{c+1},…,d X̄_n. Empty bases are allowed.

If B is smooth over A, then for every prime q⊆B there is g∈B\q such that B_g is standard smooth over A. A finite family of such elements g can be chosen to generate the unit ideal of B, allowing the empty cover for the zero algebra.

Smooth A-algebras are preserved by composition of compatible maps and arbitrary base change. If B is smooth over A and g∈B, then B_g is smooth over A. If a∈A already maps to a unit in B, then the induced A_a→B is smooth.

For any A-algebra B, without an initial finite-presentation assumption, if g_1,…,g_m∈B generate the unit ideal and every B_{g_i} is smooth over A, then B is smooth over A. This includes the empty family in the zero algebra.
An A-algebra B is smooth over A at a prime q⊆B if B_g is smooth over A for some g∈B\q. The smooth locus is the set of such primes.

If B is finitely presented over A, then for every prime q⊆B the following are equivalent: B is smooth over A at q; B_q is formally smooth over A; the localized conormal map of a finite polynomial presentation of B has a left inverse over B_q. The smooth locus is open. For any A-algebra B, smoothness is equivalent to smoothness at every prime, and equivalent to the existence of finitely many principal localizations B_{g_i} that are standard smooth over A with the g_i generating the unit ideal.
Every smooth A-algebra B is flat as an A-module, for arbitrary commutative base ring A.

For B smooth over A, define r_{B/A}(q)=dim_{κ(q)}(κ(q)⊗_B Ω_{B/A}) for every q∈Spec B. This function is locally constant and equals n−c on each standard smooth chart with n variables and c relations. For arbitrary A→A′, B′=A′⊗_A B, and a prime q′∈Spec B′ contracting to q∈Spec B, r_{B′/A′}(q′)=r_{B/A}(q). For compatible smooth maps A→B→C and a prime r∈Spec C contracting to q∈Spec B, r_{C/A}(r)=r_{B/A}(q)+r_{C/B}(r).

Let B=P/I be finitely presented over A, where P=A[X_1,…,X_n]. Let Q∈Spec P contain I, put q=Q/I, and choose f_1,…,f_c∈I whose classes are a κ(q)-basis of I_Q/(Q P_Q)I_Q. Then B is smooth at q if and only if the partial-derivative matrix of these f_j has column rank c over κ(q). In particular, the full-column-rank criterion applies to any prescribed equation list at primes where that list minimally generates I_Q; the minimality hypothesis is part of this assertion.

Standard smoothness is preserved by composition, arbitrary base change, and principal localization of the target. In the corresponding displayed presentations, n−c adds under composition and remains unchanged under base change and principal localization.

If B has a standard smooth presentation over A with n variables and c relations, then for every ring map A→F to a field such that F⊗_A B is nonzero, the field fiber F⊗_A B has Krull dimension n−c. After extending F to an algebraic closure, all local rings at closed points of that fiber are regular local rings of dimension n−c. No assertion of dimension n−c is imposed on a zero fiber.

Let B be finitely presented over A, let A→A′ be flat, and put B′=A′⊗_A B. The smooth locus of B′ over A′ equals the inverse image of the smooth locus of B over A under Spec B′→Spec B. Equivalently, for each prime q′ of B′ with contraction q, B′/A′ is smooth at q′ if and only if B/A is smooth at q.
For any finite family of A-algebras, its product is smooth over A if and only if each factor is smooth over A. The empty product is the zero algebra, and it is smooth over A.
For every smooth A-algebra B, there exist a finitely generated ℤ-subalgebra A_0⊆A and a smooth A_0-algebra B_0 such that B≅A⊗_{A_0}B_0 as A-algebras.

For every ideal J⊆A and every smooth A/J-algebra C, there is a finite cover of Spec C by principal opens whose localized algebras are standard smooth over A/J, and for each such chart there is a standard smooth A-algebra whose reduction modulo J is isomorphic to that chart. The covering elements generate the unit ideal of C.

A polynomial A-algebra in finitely many variables is standard smooth via its presentation with no equations. For every a∈A, A[T]/(aT−1) is standard smooth of relative rank zero, since a becomes a unit in this quotient. These assertions include the zero-algebra boundary cases.

For b∈A, put B=A[X,Y]/(XY−b). The principal localizations on D(X̄) and D(Ȳ) are standard smooth over A of relative rank 1. When A=k is a field and b=0, B is not smooth at the origin (the prime/maximal ideal (X̄,Ȳ)): the one relation XY minimally generates the localized nonzero relation ideal, but both derivatives vanish at that point.

For a field k of characteristic p>0, let B=k[X]/(X^p). The B-module Ω_{B/k} is free of rank 1 on d X̄, but B is not smooth over k. More explicitly, the identity B→k[X]/(X^p) has no k-algebra lift through k[X]/(X^{p+1})↠k[X]/(X^p), whose kernel is square-zero. Any proposed image of X̄ is X+λX^p modulo X^{p+1} with λ∈k, and its p-th power is X^p≠0, violating the relation X̄^p=0.

The pointwise full-column-rank Jacobian test requires equations that minimally generate the localized relation ideal; redundant equations may cause the full matrix to lose column rank although the algebra is smooth. For example (X,X²)=(X) in A[X], and A[X]/(X)≅A is smooth over A, while the redundant two-equation presentation is not a test for the number of independent relations; the pointwise criterion uses the single relation X here.

The general smooth-fiber criterion and its use for geometrically regular fibers are deferred to the scheme-theoretic continuation. The next chapter will use the conormal criterion, flatness, and rank-zero Jacobian presentations; these sentences specify scope and routing, not an additional theorem.

The closing citations point to the two-term cotangent complex, original finite-presentation formulations, and Eisenbud’s differential Jacobian matrix. They are bibliographic context and do not add the full cotangent complex to the required scope.

Chapter roadmap: finite presentation permits a polynomial description and testing on principal neighborhoods of the square-zero unique-lifting property; square Jacobian, local one-variable forms, and fibers over fields are developed below. This is introductory context, with the mathematical obligations stated separately.

For a commutative unital ring A and specified A-algebra B, B is étale over A if B is finitely presented as an A-algebra and formally étale. B is unramified over A if B is of finite type and formally unramified. Finitely presented unramified means formally unramified with finite presentation, rather than merely finite type. Zero rings are allowed throughout.

For every A-algebra B, the following are equivalent: (i) B/A is étale; (ii) B/A is smooth and Ω_{B/A}=0; (iii) B is finitely presented and, for one polynomial A-algebra presentation P↠B with kernel I, the conormal map I/I²→B⊗_PΩ_{P/A} is an isomorphism. In (iii), one polynomial presentation can equivalently be replaced by every polynomial presentation.

An A-algebra B is étale over A if and only if, for some integer n≥0 and polynomials f₁,…,fₙ∈A[X₁,…,Xₙ], there is an A-algebra isomorphism B≅A[X₁,…,Xₙ]/(f₁,…,fₙ) such that the image of det((∂fⱼ/∂Xᵢ)ᵢⱼ) is a unit of B. For n=0 the empty determinant is 1; this case is included.

Étaleness is preserved by arbitrary base change (if B/A is étale and A→A′ any ring map, A′⊗_A B is étale over A′), by composition of compatible étale maps A→B→C, and by principal localization in the target (B_b/A is étale for b∈B whenever B/A is étale). For any A-algebra B and finite list b₁,…,bᵣ∈B generating the unit ideal, if every B_{bᵢ}/A is étale then B/A is étale, including the empty-cover zero-ring case.
If B is finitely presented over A, its étale locus, the set of primes q∈Spec(B) for which some b∉q has B_b/A étale, is open and equals the set of smooth primes of B/A minus Supp_B(Ω_{B/A}).
For a B-module M, Supp_B(M)={q∈Spec(B) | M_q≠0}.
For a compatible tower A→B→C, if B/A is formally unramified and C/A is formally étale, then C/B is formally étale. If B/A and C/A are both étale, then C/B is étale.
A standard étale A-algebra is an A-algebra admitting a presentation (A[X]/(f))_g with f∈A[X] monic, g∈A[X], and the image of the formal derivative f′ invertible in this localized quotient.
For a prime q of an A-algebra B, B/A is étale at q if there exists b∈B\q such that B_b is étale over A.

For arbitrary f,g∈A[X], if the image of f′ is a unit in (A[X]/(f))_g, then this localized quotient is étale over A; monicity is not required for this assertion. In particular every standard étale algebra is étale. Principal localization of a standard étale A-algebra remains standard étale over A, and arbitrary base change A→A′ of a standard étale A-algebra is standard étale over A′.

For every ideal I⊆A, A→A/I is formally étale if and only if I²=I, and is étale if and only if I=Ae for some idempotent e∈A (e²=e). In the latter case there is an A-algebra isomorphism A/I≅A_{1−e}. This includes I=0 and I=A.

If B is finitely presented over A and étale at q∈Spec(B), there exists b∈B\q such that B_b is standard étale over A. If B/A is étale, the resulting principal neighborhoods cover Spec(B) and admit a finite subcover, including the empty spectrum.

For field extensions L/K: every separable algebraic extension, without a finiteness hypothesis, is formally étale; if L/K is finite, it is étale if and only if separable; more generally, if L/K is finitely generated as a field extension, formal unramifiedness is equivalent to L/K being finite separable.

For a finite-type algebra B over a field K, the following are equivalent: Ω_{B/K}=0; B/K is étale; B is isomorphic as a K-algebra to a finite product of finite separable field extensions of K. The empty product is permitted and equals the zero ring.
For any A-algebra B, B/A is étale if and only if B is finitely presented as an A-algebra, flat as an A-module, and Ω_{B/A}=0.

If an A-algebra B is étale at q∈Spec(B), and p is the inverse image of q in A, then qB_q=pB_q and the induced field extension κ(q)/κ(p) is finite separable. No global finite-presentation assumption on B is imposed beyond having an étale principal neighborhood.

If B/A is étale and D=B⊗_A B, the multiplication map μ:D→B is, up to a canonical isomorphism of D-algebras, localization at an idempotent element of D. Equivalently there is an idempotent e∈D with ker(μ)=De and B≅D_{1−e} as D-algebras. Thus the associated affine diagonal is open and closed.

For any ring map A→A′ and B′=A′⊗_A B: if A′ is faithfully flat over A and B′/A′ is étale, then B/A is étale. If B is finitely presented over A and A′ is flat over A, then for every q′∈Spec(B′), B′/A′ is étale at q′ if and only if B/A is étale at the inverse image q∈Spec(B). Equivalently the étale locus of B′/A′ is the inverse image of the étale locus of B/A.

Every étale A-algebra B has a model over a finitely generated ℤ-algebra: there exist a finitely generated ℤ-algebra A₀, a ring map A₀→A, and an étale A₀-algebra B₀ with B≅A⊗_{A₀}B₀ as A-algebras. More generally, if A is the filtered colimit of rings Aᵢ, every étale A-algebra B is isomorphic to A⊗_{Aᵢ}Bᵢ for some stage i and some étale Aᵢ-algebra Bᵢ. If A=S⁻¹A₀, a model can be taken over (A₀)_s for some s∈S.

For any a∈A, A→A_a is étale and A_a≅A[X]/(aX−1), whose Jacobian a is a unit in the quotient. An arbitrary localization S⁻¹A/A is formally étale but need not be of finite type: in particular ℚ is not of finite type as a ℤ-algebra, since finitely many rational generators involve only finitely many denominator primes.
If 2 and a are units in A, then A[X]/(X²−a) is étale over A; the image of its derivative 2X is a unit in the quotient.

For every prime integer p, the canonical quotient ℤ→𝔽_p is finitely presented and unramified but is not flat and hence not étale. Indeed tensoring the injective multiplication-by-p map ℤ→ℤ with 𝔽_p gives the zero map on the nonzero module 𝔽_p.

For every field k, B=k[ε]/(ε²) has nonzero Ω_{B/k}, including in characteristic two, so B/k is not unramified or étale. Regarded instead as a k[X]-algebra through X↦ε, B has zero relative differentials and kernel (X²), which is not idempotent; this quotient map is unramified but not formally étale or étale. These are distinct conclusions for the two specified base maps.
For any finite family of A-algebras (Bᵢ), the product ∏ᵢBᵢ is étale over A if and only if every Bᵢ is étale over A. This includes the empty product, the zero A-algebra, which is étale.

Let B be finitely presented over A, q∈Spec(B), and p=q∩A. Then B/A is étale at q if and only if all three hold: B_q is flat as an A_p-module; pB_q=qB_q; κ(q)/κ(p) is a finite separable field extension. In particular, for every p∈Spec(A), the fiber B⊗_Aκ(p) of an étale algebra is a finite product of finite separable extensions of κ(p), allowing the empty product zero fiber.
For every ideal I⊆A and every étale A/I-algebra B̄, there exists an étale A-algebra B and an A/I-algebra isomorphism B/IB≅B̄.
For every p∈Spec(A) and every finite separable field extension L/κ(p), there exist an étale A-algebra B and a prime q∈Spec(B) lying over p such that κ(q)≅L as κ(p)-algebras.

The canonical field extension 𝔽₂→𝔽₄ and the diagonal map 𝔽₄→𝔽₄⁴ are standard étale, presented respectively by X²+X+1 and ∏_{a∈𝔽₄}(X−a). Their composite 𝔽₂→𝔽₄⁴ is étale but has no single standard étale presentation over 𝔽₂. The obstruction is that a localized one-variable quotient over 𝔽₂ can have at most one prime with residue field 𝔽₄, since X²+X+1 is the unique monic irreducible quadratic over 𝔽₂, whereas 𝔽₄⁴ has four such primes.

The localization comparison for Kähler differentials on principal opens, determined by db↦d(b/1), is compatible with iterated localization. The differential base-change comparison A′⊗_AΩ_{B/A}≅Ω_{(A′⊗_A B)/A′} is compatible with these principal-localization restriction maps.

The comparisons above are inputs for constructing the relative differential sheaf on affine charts. Previously established smooth/étale local forms provide the corresponding charts, and the prior pointwise differential and residue-field results supply their fibers. This is a transition to a separate geometric formulation, not an additional construction of a sheaf in this source scope.

Chapter roadmap: regular sequences control quotients by Koszul resolutions and associated graded modules, and Koszul homology will be used for depth. The separately stated results below carry these mathematical obligations.

Let R be a commutative unital ring, M an R-module, and x=(x₁,…,xᵣ) an ordered finite list. Put Iⱼ=(x₁,…,xⱼ) and I₀=0. The list is weakly M-regular if multiplication by xⱼ is injective on M/I_{j−1}M for every 1≤j≤r. It is M-regular if it is weakly M-regular and M/IᵣM≠0. A regular sequence in R means an R-regular sequence.

The empty list is weakly regular on every module M and is M-regular exactly when M≠0. Every list is weakly regular on the zero module and no list is regular on it. A list beginning with a unit is weakly regular (all subsequent quotients vanish) but is not regular. Every intermediate quotient M/IⱼM of an M-regular list is nonzero.

For arbitrary R and M, an ordered concatenation (x,y) is weakly M-regular if and only if x is weakly M-regular and y is weakly regular on M/(x)M. It is M-regular if and only if x is M-regular and y is regular on M/(x)M.

Given a ring map R→S and an S-module N flat over R, every weakly M-regular list x remains weakly regular on M⊗_R N, both as a list from R and through its image in S. It is regular on M⊗_R N if the final quotient is nonzero. If N is faithfully flat over R, weak regularity and regularity are also reflected from M⊗_R N to M. In particular, if M is finite, p∈Spec(R) contains (x), M_p≠0, and x is M-regular, the localized list is M_p-regular over R_p.

For every field k and R=k[X,Y,Z], (X,Y(1−X),Z(1−X)) is an R-regular list, but the permuted list (Y(1−X),Z(1−X),X) is not weakly regular: the class of Y in R/(Y(1−X)) is nonzero and is annihilated by Z(1−X). Thus regularity need not survive permutation over a nonlocal ring.

For any R-linear map u:E→R with E an arbitrary R-module, construct the nonnegative homological Koszul complex K(u) with K_q(u)=∧^q_R E and differential d(e₁∧⋯∧e_q)=Σ_{i=1}^q(−1)^{i−1}u(eᵢ)e₁∧⋯∧êᵢ∧⋯∧e_q. For x=(x₁,…,xᵣ), K(x) means E=R^r with u(eᵢ)=xᵢ. For coefficients M, set K(x;M)=K(x)⊗_R M and let H_q(x;M) denote homology. For the empty list K(x;M) is M concentrated in degree 0.

The Koszul contraction formula is multilinear and alternating, including in characteristic two, and satisfies d²=0. It obeys the graded Leibniz rule d(a∧b)=da∧b+(−1)^p a∧db for a of exterior degree p. For a list x of length r, K_q(x) is finite free with the increasing q-fold standard wedges as basis and rank binomial(r,q); in particular it vanishes for q>r. For every coefficient module M, H₀(x;M)≅M/(x)M.

For linear maps u:E→R and u′:E′→R and an R-linear φ:E→E′ with u′∘φ=u, the exterior powers ∧^qφ define a chain map K(u)→K(u′), respecting identities and composition. For every ring map R→S there is a natural isomorphism of complexes S⊗_R K(u)≅K(S⊗_R u), with S⊗_R u understood as S⊗_R E→S. Consequently permutations and invertible linear changes of a generating list induce isomorphic Koszul complexes. If S is flat over R, S⊗_R H_q(x;M)≅H_q(image(x);S⊗_R M) naturally for all q.

For R-linear u:E→R and v:F→R, K(u⊕v)≅K(u)⊗_R K(v), where (u⊕v)(e,f)=u(e)+v(f) and the total differential is d(a⊗b)=da⊗b+(−1)^{deg(a)}a⊗db. For a list x, element y∈R, and R-module M, K(x,y;M) is isomorphic to the mapping cone of multiplication by y on C=K(x;M). It yields a natural long exact homology sequence whose segment is H_q(C)→[y]H_q(C)→H_q(x,y;M)→H_{q−1}(C)→[y]H_{q−1}(C), for every degree q.

For any list x of length r, ideal I=(x), and module M, multiplication by every a∈I on K(x;M) is chain-homotopic to zero. Thus I annihilates all Koszul homology H_q(x;M) and coefficient Koszul cohomology H^q(x;M). If I=R, K(x;M) is contractible. If a₁,…,a_s∈I, then K(x,a₁,…,a_s;M)≅K(x;M)⊗_R∧^•R^s as complexes, with zero differential on ∧^•R^s. If M/IM≠0, r−max{q | H_q(x;M)≠0} depends only on I and M, independently of the chosen finite generating list x.

For any R-module M and weakly M-regular list x, H_q(x;M)=0 for every q>0. If x is an R-regular list of length r, the augmentation K(x)→R/(x) is a finite free resolution of length r; for every R-module M and q≥0 there is an isomorphism H_q(x;M)≅Tor_q^R(R/(x),M). If x is both R-regular and weakly M-regular, these Tor groups vanish for all q>0.

Let R be Noetherian, M a finite R-module, and x a finite list all of whose entries lie in Jac(R). If H₁(x;M)=0 then x is weakly M-regular; if additionally M≠0 it is M-regular. In particular for every nonzero finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m) and every finite list x in m, the following are equivalent: x is M-regular; H_q(x;M)=0 for all q>0; H₁(x;M)=0.

For a nonzero finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), every permutation of an M-regular list in m is M-regular. Over an arbitrary ring, replacing any entries of a weakly M-regular list by positive integer powers preserves weak regularity, and preserves regularity if the original list is M-regular. More generally, if two lists differing only by replacing one entry a by b are both weakly M-regular, their list with that entry replaced by ab is weakly M-regular; if both original lists are M-regular, the product list is M-regular. In the nonzero finite Noetherian local case, every M-regular list in m is a minimal generating list of its ideal I, and every other minimal generating list of I is M-regular.

For a length-r list x over R, put E=R^r, D=∧^r_R E, and D∨=Hom_R(D,R). Give Hom_R(K(x),M) the cochain differential δ(f)=f∘d. There is an isomorphism of cochain complexes Hom_R(K(x),M)^q≅K_{r−q}(x;M⊗_R D∨), with differential d on the reversed indexing. Orienting E by its ordered basis gives H^q(x;M)≅H_{r−q}(x;M). If x is R-regular and I=(x), this cochain complex computes Ext_R^q(R/I,M); for M=R, Ext_R^q(R/I,R)=0 for q≠r and the orientation identifies Ext_R^r(R/I,R) with R/I.
For an ideal I=(x₁,…,xᵣ) of R and an R-module M, define the I-associated graded module gr_I M=⊕_{n≥0} I^nM/I^{n+1}M. For M=R this is a graded algebra over R/I.

For any ring R, R-module M, and finite list x=(x₁,…,xᵣ) with I=(x), evaluation at the initial classes of the xᵢ defines a graded surjection (M/IM)[X₁,…,Xᵣ]→gr_I M of (R/I)[X₁,…,Xᵣ]-modules. If x is weakly M-regular, this map is an isomorphism. In the ring case M=R it is then an isomorphism of graded algebras. In particular, for an R-regular list, I/I² is free over R/I with basis the classes of x₁,…,xᵣ.
The list x=(x₁,…,xᵣ), with I=(x), is M-quasi-regular if the graded evaluation map (M/IM)[X₁,…,Xᵣ]→gr_I M is an isomorphism and M/IM≠0.

For a ring R, an R-module M, a finite list x=(x₁,…,xᵣ), and I=(x), suppose the successive modules M, M/x₁M, …, M/(x₁,…,x_{r−1})M are I-adically separated: the intersection of their I^n multiples over n≥0 is zero. If x is M-quasi-regular, then x is M-regular. In particular, if (R,m) is Noetherian local, M is finite and nonzero, and I⊆m, the following four conditions are equivalent: x is M-quasi-regular; x is M-regular; H_q(x;M)=0 for every q>0; H₁(x;M)=0.

For a polynomial A-algebra presentation P↠B=P/I whose kernel I is generated by a P-regular list, the relation classes form a B-basis of I/I², but the conormal map I/I²→B⊗_PΩ_{P/A} need not be injective or split injective. Specifically for every field k, X² is regular in P=k[X], and for B=k[X]/(X²) the nonzero class of X² generates I/I² and maps to 2X dX. Multiplication of that class by the nonzero element X̄ produces a nonzero element with image zero, even when 2 is invertible in k. Thus regular relations alone do not imply the formal-smoothness split conormal criterion.

For any fixed finite list x over R, a short exact sequence 0→L→M→N→0 of coefficient modules induces short exact sequences of Koszul chain complexes and coefficient cochain complexes, hence natural long exact Koszul homology and cohomology sequences. If x is weakly regular on every term C_i of an exact complex of R-modules C, the reduced complex with terms C_i/(x)C_i is exact. In a short exact sequence 0→L→M→N→0, if x is weakly regular on L and N then it is weakly regular on M.

For every nonzero ring A and every r≥0, in R=A[X₁,…,Xᵣ] the variables (X₁,…,Xᵣ) are an R-regular list. The successive quotients are polynomial rings in the remaining variables. Its Koszul complex is a finite free resolution of A as an R-module, with A acted on through evaluation of all variables at zero. With this A also as coefficient module all differentials vanish, and H_q((X₁,…,Xᵣ);A)≅∧^q_A A^r for every q≥0.

For a field k, R=k[ε]/(ε²), and x=(ε), K(x) has the single boundary map R→R given by multiplication by ε; H₁(x;R)=(ε) and H₀(x;R)≅k. Thus a nonzero nilpotent can yield nonzero positive Koszul homology.
For any ring R, coefficient module M, and finite list containing a unit, the entire Koszul complex K(x;M) is contractible.

A finite list generating a proper ideal whose Koszul complex is acyclic in every positive degree need not be regular in its given order outside the local hypotheses: in R=k[X,Y,Z] over any field k, x=(Y(1−X),Z(1−X),X) generates a proper ideal, has H_q(x;R)=0 for every q>0, but is not weakly R-regular, as in the earlier order counterexample.

For every finite list x of length r over R, I=(x), and R-module M, the ordered basis identifies H_r(x;M) with the annihilator 0:_M I, and H^0(x;M) with Hom_R(R/I,M). Homology is zero outside degrees 0,…,r. If y∈I acts injectively on M, there are short exact sequences 0→H_q(x;M)→H_q(x;M/yM)→H_{q−1}(x;M)→0 for every degree q, using zero homology outside the stated range. More generally, if M/IM≠0 and y₁,…,y_s∈I form an M-regular sequence, then s≤r, H_q(x;M)=0 for q>r−s, and H_{r−s}(x;M)≅0:_{M/(y₁,…,y_s)M}I. Empty lists and s=0 are included.

For arbitrary R, R-module M, and finite list x generating I, H₁(x;M)=0 implies that the evaluation map (M/IM)[X₁,…,Xᵣ]→gr_I M is an isomorphism, without finiteness or separation assumptions and without requiring M/IM≠0. Both degree-one Koszul acyclicity (H₁=0) and positive-degree acyclicity (H_q=0 for all q>0) are preserved when any coordinate is replaced by a positive integer power. More generally, for two lists differing only by values a and b of a fixed coordinate, if both lists satisfy either one of these acyclicity conditions, the list with that coordinate ab satisfies that same condition.

Chapter overview and bibliography: regular-sequence lengths, Ext and Koszul vanishing thresholds, relative grade, and finite projective dimension are the topics. This is an organizational introduction; its mathematical content is stated precisely in the results below.

For a Noetherian commutative ring R, finite R-module M, and ideal I, define grade_R(I,M)=+∞ if IM=M; otherwise define it as the supremum of the lengths of finite M-regular sequences all of whose entries lie in I, with the regular-sequence convention of Chapter 5 (successive multiplication is injective and the terminal quotient is nonzero). For a Noetherian local ring (R,m,k), define depth_R M=grade_R(m,M). In particular depth_R 0=+∞.

Let R be Noetherian, M a finite R-module, and I an ideal with IM≠M. The following are equivalent: grade_R(I,M)=0; there exists p∈Ass_R(M) with I⊆p; the submodule (0:_M I) is nonzero. Consequently, for a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), depth_R M=0 iff its socle (0:_M m) is nonzero.
Let (R,m) be Noetherian local and M a nonzero finite R-module. If x∈m acts injectively on M, then dim Supp_R(M/xM)=dim Supp_R(M)−1. Moreover depth_R M≤dim Supp_R(M).
For every Noetherian ring R, finite R-module M, and ideal I with IM≠M, there is a finite uniform upper bound on the lengths of M-regular sequences in I.
For finite modules N,M over a Noetherian ring R, Hom_R(N,M)≠0 iff Supp_R(N)∩Ass_R(M) is nonempty.

For any commutative ring R, any R-modules N,M, every i≥0 and a∈R, the scalar action of a on Ext_R^i(N,M) induced contravariantly by multiplication by a on N agrees with the action induced covariantly by multiplication by a on M. In particular Ann_R(N) annihilates Ext_R^i(N,M). No Noetherian or finite-generation hypotheses are imposed in this assertion.

Let R be Noetherian and N,M finite R-modules. Then grade_R(Ann_R(N),M)=inf{i≥0 | Ext_R^i(N,M)≠0}, with inf ∅=+∞. In particular for any ideal I, grade_R(I,M)=inf{i≥0 | Ext_R^i(R/I,M)≠0}; in a Noetherian local ring (R,m,k), depth_R M=inf{i≥0 | Ext_R^i(k,M)≠0}. These conventions include zero modules and IM=M.
Let R be Noetherian, M a finite R-module, and I an ideal with IM≠M. Every maximal M-regular sequence in I has length grade_R(I,M).

Let R be Noetherian and N,M finite R-modules. If x_1,…,x_r is M-regular, each x_i belongs to Ann_R(N), and J=(x_1,…,x_r), then Ext_R^i(N,M)=0 for 0≤i<r and there is a natural isomorphism Ext_R^r(N,M)≅Hom_R(N,M/JM). The sequence need not be maximal; the empty sequence r=0 is included.

Let R be Noetherian, M finite, and I an ideal with IM≠M. For an M-regular sequence x_1,…,x_r in I, put J=(x_1,…,x_r). Then grade_{R/J}(I/J,M/JM)=grade_R(I,M/JM)=grade_R(I,M)−r. In the local case, when the sequence is in the maximal ideal, depth_{R/J}(M/JM)=depth_R M−r.

Let R be Noetherian, M a finite R-module, I an ideal of R, and A an ideal annihilating M. Writing Ī=(I+A)/A for the image ideal of R/A, one has grade_R(I,M)=grade_{R/A}(Ī,M), including the case of infinite grade.
For a nonzero finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m,k), put d=depth_R M and define type_R(M)=dim_k Ext_R^d(k,M).

For a nonzero finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m,k), if x_1,…,x_d is any maximal M-regular sequence in m and J=(x_1,…,x_d), then type_R(M)=dim_k(0:_{M/JM}m). In particular this socle dimension is independent of the chosen maximal sequence and equals dim_k Ext_R^d(k,M), where d=depth_R M.
For a Noetherian ring R, finite R-module M, and ideal I, grade_R(I,M)=inf{depth_{R_p}(M_p) | p∈V(I)∩Supp_R(M)}. The infimum of the empty set is +∞.
For R Noetherian, M finite, and ideals I,J, grade_R(I,M)=grade_R(√I,M), and grade_R(IJ,M)=grade_R(I∩J,M)=min(grade_R(I,M),grade_R(J,M)), with +∞ allowed. For every proper ideal I, grade_R(I,R)≤ht(I).

Fix an ideal I of a Noetherian ring R and a short exact sequence 0→L→M→N→0 of finite R-modules. Set a=grade_R(I,L), b=grade_R(I,M), c=grade_R(I,N). Then b≥min(a,c), a≥min(b,c+1), and c≥min(b,a−1), where subtraction by one at zero is zero and +∞±1=+∞. These statements hold also for local depths. Moreover a<c implies b=a; a>c+1 implies b=c; and a<b implies a≥1 and c=a−1.
Let R,S be Noetherian rings, I an ideal of R, M a finite R-module, and R→S a flat ring map. Then grade_R(I,M)≤grade_S(IS,S⊗_R M); equality holds if R→S is faithfully flat, including infinite grades.

Let R,S be Noetherian rings, S a finite R-algebra, I an ideal of R, and N a finite S-module. Then grade_R(I,N)=grade_S(IS,N), with N on the left viewed by restriction of scalars. If (R,m) is local, depth_R N=inf{depth_{S_n}(N_n) | n a maximal ideal of S}. The empty infimum is +∞, and if S≠0 the infimum is attained.

For a Noetherian ring R, finite R-module M, and generating list a=(a_1,…,a_n) of I, form the Koszul cochain complex K^i(a;M)=Hom_R(K_i(a;R),M), with differential induced by the Koszul differential of the homological Koszul complex of Chapter 5.

Let R be Noetherian, M finite, and I=(a_1,…,a_n). For the Koszul cochain complex K^i(a;M)=Hom_R(K_i(a;R),M), grade_R(I,M)=inf{i≥0 | H^i(K•(a;M))≠0}=n−sup{j≥0 | H_j(K•(a;M))≠0}. When the complexes are acyclic both thresholds are +∞. If M/IM≠0 then grade_R(I,M)≤n. The first nonvanishing cohomological degree is independent of the chosen finite generating list of I, although the cohomology groups themselves can depend on the list.
Let (R,m) be Noetherian local and M a nonzero finite R-module. For every associated prime p∈Ass_R(M), depth_R M≤dim(R/p).
Let (R,m) be Noetherian local and M a nonzero finite R-module. For every prime p of R, depth_R M≤depth_{R_p}(M_p)+dim(R/p), including primes outside Supp_R(M), where depth_{R_p}(0)=+∞.

Depth may strictly decrease under localization: there exist a Noetherian local ring R, a nonzero finite R-module M and a prime p∈Supp_R(M) with depth_{R_p}(M_p)<depth_R(M). Depth may also strictly increase: there exist (possibly different) such R, M and p with depth_{R_p}(M_p)>depth_R(M).
If R is Noetherian local and N,M are nonzero finite R-modules, then Ext_R^i(N,M)=0 for every integer i satisfying 0≤i<depth_R M−dim Supp_R(N).

Let R be any Noetherian ring, E a finite R-module, g=grade_R(Ann_R(E),R), and N a finite R-module of finite projective dimension ℓ. Then Ext_R^i(E,N)=0 for 0≤i<g−ℓ. If g=+∞ this means vanishing in every nonnegative degree.
For a nonzero finite module E over a Noetherian ring R, grade_R(Ann_R(E),R)≤pd_R(E), including pd_R(E)=+∞.

For every finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m,k), there exists a free resolution F•→M such that every F_i is finite free and im(F_{i+1}→F_i)⊆mF_i for every i≥0. Such a resolution is the minimal free resolution in this chapter; M=0 is allowed.

For a minimal free resolution F•→M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m,k), with finite free terms and im(F_{i+1}→F_i)⊆mF_i, one has k⊗_R F_i≅Tor_i^R(k,M) for every i≥0. If M≠0 has finite projective dimension e, then F_e≠0 and F_i=0 for all i>e: its last nonzero term is exactly F_e.

Let (R,m,k) be Noetherian local and M a nonzero finite R-module of finite projective dimension e. Then pd_R M+depth_R M=depth_R R. If x∈m acts injectively on M, then pd_R(M/xM)=e+1. If x also acts injectively on R, then pd_{R/(x)}(M/xM)=e.

Let R be commutative, x an element acting injectively on both R and an R-module M, S=R/(x), and N any S-module. Then Hom_R(N,M)=0 and for every j≥0 there is a natural isomorphism Ext_R^{j+1}(N,M)≅Ext_S^j(N,M/xM). For a finite sequence x_1,…,x_r regular on both R and M and N killed by J=(x_1,…,x_r), this iterates to natural isomorphisms Ext_R^{j+r}(N,M)≅Ext_{R/J}^j(N,M/JM) for j≥0, with vanishing in degrees below r. No Noetherian or finite-module assumption is imposed in the one-element statement or its iteration.

For a Noetherian ring R, ideal I, and finite R-module M, grade_R(I,M)≥2 iff the restriction map Hom_R(R,M)→Hom_R(I,M) induced by I↪R is an isomorphism. Under evaluation at 1, Hom_R(R,M) is identified with M; equivalently every R-linear map I→M has a unique extension to R.

Chapter introduction and bibliography: the Cohen–Macaulay equality between depth and support dimension permits analysis of parameters, associated primes, and localizations using Chapter 6. It introduces no separate theorem beyond the following precise statements.

For a nonzero finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), put d_R(M)=dim Supp_R(M)=dim(R/Ann_R(M)). Define M to be Cohen–Macaulay if depth_R M=d_R(M), and maximal Cohen–Macaulay if depth_R M=dim R. A ring is Cohen–Macaulay at a prime p if R_p is Cohen–Macaulay as a module over itself. For a Noetherian ring, a finite module is globally Cohen–Macaulay if M_p is Cohen–Macaulay over R_p for every p∈Supp_R(M); a Cohen–Macaulay ring has this property for M=R. The zero module is Cohen–Macaulay locally and globally by convention, and is admitted along with nonzero maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules in syzygy assertions. Numerical assertions for nonzero modules use their nonzero support.
Let M be a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), and let J⊆m be an ideal. Then Supp_R(M/JM)=Supp_R(M)∩V(J), and M/JM has finite length iff this support is exactly {m}.

For a nonzero finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), with d=d_R(M), a system of parameters is a sequence of d elements of m whose quotient on M has finite length. The empty sequence is allowed when d=0.
For a nonzero finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), systems of parameters exist, and d_R(M) is the minimum length of any finite sequence in m whose quotient on M has finite length.
Let M be a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian local ring (R,m) and x∈m act injectively on M. Then d_R(M/xM)=d_R(M)−1.

Let M be a nonzero finite Cohen–Macaulay module over a Noetherian local ring R. Every p∈Ass_R(M) satisfies dim(R/p)=d_R(M) and is minimal in Supp_R(M). All minimal primes in Supp_R(M) are associated. Thus all irreducible components of Supp_R(M) have dimension d_R(M), and M has no embedded associated primes.

Let M be a nonzero finite Cohen–Macaulay module over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), set d=d_R(M), and let x_1,…,x_c be a finite sequence in m. It is M-regular iff d_R(M/(x_1,…,x_c)M)=d−c. In either case the sequence extends to a system of parameters for M, and every intermediate quotient M/(x_1,…,x_i)M, 0≤i≤c, is Cohen–Macaulay. Subtraction here is the ordinary dimension drop; the criterion does not permit natural-number truncation when c>d, and includes c=0.

For a nonzero finite module M over a Noetherian local ring, the following are equivalent: M is Cohen–Macaulay; some system of parameters for M is M-regular; every system of parameters for M is M-regular. The dimension-zero case and empty system of parameters are included.

Let M be nonzero and finite over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), and let x∈m be M-regular. Then M is Cohen–Macaulay iff M/xM is Cohen–Macaulay; the quotient module may be viewed over either R or R/(x).

Let R→S be a surjective local map of Noetherian local rings and M a finite S-module. Viewed as an R-module or an S-module, M has the same support dimension and the same depth. Consequently its Cohen–Macaulay property is independent of these two scalar structures; the zero module is included with the stated conventions.
Let (R,m) be Noetherian local and M a nonzero finite Cohen–Macaulay R-module. For every p∈Supp_R(M), M_p is Cohen–Macaulay over R_p and d_R(M)=d_{R_p}(M_p)+dim(R/p).

For a finite module M over a Noetherian ring R, global Cohen–Macaulayness is equivalent to Cohen–Macaulayness of M_m over R_m for all maximal ideals m in its support. If M is globally Cohen–Macaulay, then U^{-1}M is Cohen–Macaulay over U^{-1}R for every multiplicative set U. This includes the zero-module convention and arbitrary localization.
If R is Noetherian and Cohen–Macaulay, then grade_R(I,R)=ht(I) for every proper ideal I. If R is also local, then ht(I)+dim(R/I)=dim R for every proper ideal I.

In a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring R, for every pair of primes p⊆q every saturated chain from p to q has length ht(q)−ht(p). Hence R is catenary. In the local case every maximal chain in Spec R has length dim R.

Every regular Noetherian local ring R is Cohen–Macaulay. If d=dim R and x₁,…,x_d minimally generate its maximal ideal, then R/(x₁,…,x_c) is regular local of dimension d−c for every 0≤c≤d. Quotients by arbitrary regular sequences in the maximal ideal are Cohen–Macaulay, and such a quotient can fail to be regular.

Let R be a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring and I a proper ideal of height c generated by a displayed list of c elements. At every maximal ideal m containing I, that list localized in R_m is an R_m-regular sequence. The ring R/I is Cohen–Macaulay, and every associated prime of R/I viewed in Spec R is minimal over I and has height c. In particular a quotient of a regular local ring by a regular sequence in its maximal ideal is Cohen–Macaulay.
Let R be Noetherian. Suppose that for every proper ideal I generated by ht(I) elements, every associated prime of R/I (as a prime of R) has height ht(I). Then R is Cohen–Macaulay.

Let (R,m,k)→(S,n) be a local map of Noetherian local rings, M a nonzero finite R-module, and N a nonzero finite S-module flat over R. Set S_0=S/mS and N_0=N/mN. Then N_0 and M⊗_R N are nonzero finite modules over their displayed local scalar rings, d_S(M⊗_R N)=d_R(M)+d_{S_0}(N_0), and depth_S(M⊗_R N)=depth_R M+depth_{S_0}(N_0). Moreover M⊗_R N is Cohen–Macaulay iff both M over R and N_0 over S_0 are Cohen–Macaulay.
For a flat local map (R,m)→S of Noetherian local rings, S is Cohen–Macaulay iff R and the closed fiber S/mS are both Cohen–Macaulay.

For a finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,m), m-adic completion preserves dimension, depth, and the Cohen–Macaulay property: for M≠0, dim Supp_{R̂}(M̂)=dim Supp_R(M) and depth_{R̂}(M̂)=depth_R(M), and M̂ is Cohen–Macaulay over R̂ iff M is Cohen–Macaulay over R. The zero module is preserved too and satisfies the Cohen–Macaulay convention.

Let R be Noetherian, M a finite R-module, and k≥0 an integer. Serre’s condition (S_k) for M means that for every p∈Supp_R(M), depth_{R_p}(M_p)≥min(k,d_{R_p}(M_p)). For a ring R use M=R. The condition is vacuous for the zero module.

A finite module M over a Noetherian ring is Cohen–Macaulay iff it satisfies (S_k) for every nonnegative integer k. It satisfies (S_1) iff it has no embedded associated primes, meaning every associated prime is minimal in its support.

Let R→S be a flat map of Noetherian rings, let q∈Spec S contract to p∈Spec R, and fix k≥0. If the local ring S_q satisfies (S_k) at every one of its primes, then R_p satisfies (S_k) at every one of its primes.
Let R→S be a flat map of Noetherian rings and fix k≥0. If R satisfies (S_k) and every fiber S⊗_R κ(p), p∈Spec R, satisfies (S_k), then S satisfies (S_k).

Let R be a Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring of dimension d and M a nonzero finite R-module of depth e. Every (d−e)th syzygy obtained by successive finite free surjections is maximal Cohen–Macaulay or zero. The zero possibility is admitted as in the chapter convention, and the 0th syzygy when e=d is M itself.
Let R be a Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring and M a nonzero finite R-module of finite projective dimension. Then M is Cohen–Macaulay iff pd_R M=grade_R(Ann_R(M),R).

Over a regular local ring the nonzero finite maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules are precisely the nonzero finite free modules. Every finite module over a regular local ring of dimension d has projective dimension at most d; its residue field has projective dimension exactly d.

Let (R,m)→(S,n) be a local map of Noetherian local rings with R regular local. Let N be a nonzero finite Cohen–Macaulay S-module. If d_S(N)=dim R+d_{S/mS}(N/mN), then N is flat over R. In particular, if S is Cohen–Macaulay and dim S=dim R+dim(S/mS), then S is flat over R. Dimension-zero base rings and empty parameter lists are included.
For every field k, the localization of k[x,y]/(y²−x³) at the maximal ideal generated by the coordinate classes x,y is a Cohen–Macaulay local ring of dimension one and is not regular.

For every field k, the localization R of k[x,y]/(x²,xy) at the maximal ideal generated by x,y has dimension one and depth zero, has an embedded associated prime (x,y) strictly above its minimal prime (x), and fails Serre’s condition (S_1). The class of x is nonzero and has annihilator exactly the maximal ideal, exhibiting that embedded prime.
Every one-dimensional reduced Noetherian ring is Cohen–Macaulay. In particular its one-dimensional local rings have depth one; its zero-dimensional localizations are fields.

Let R be Noetherian and M a finite R-module. For every finite number r≥0 of variables, M⊗_R R[T_1,…,T_r] is Cohen–Macaulay over R[T_1,…,T_r] iff M is Cohen–Macaulay over R; likewise M⊗_R R[[T_1,…,T_r]] is Cohen–Macaulay over the formal power series ring iff M is Cohen–Macaulay over R. These are global module conditions and include M=0 and the empty-variable case.
Every Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay ring R is universally catenary: every finitely generated R-algebra is catenary.

Let R be a Noetherian algebra over a field k and let K/k be an arbitrary field extension. Assume either that R is of finite type over k or that K is finitely generated as a field extension of k. Then R⊗_k K is Noetherian and is Cohen–Macaulay iff R is Cohen–Macaulay. No separability hypothesis is imposed.

Let R be Noetherian local and I,J proper ideals with incomparable radicals (neither √I⊆√J nor √J⊆√I). If I∩J is a nilpotent ideal, then grade_R(I+J,R)≤1. If R additionally satisfies (S_2), in particular if R is Cohen–Macaulay, then ht(I+J)≤1.

For a Noetherian local ring R satisfying (S_2), in particular for a local Cohen–Macaulay ring, any partition of its minimal irreducible components into two disjoint nonempty families has unions meeting in codimension at most one. More precisely, if I and J are the intersections of the minimal primes in the two families, then their union-intersection locus is V(I+J) and ht(I+J)≤1; their two unions cannot meet only in codimension at least two.
If A is Noetherian and Cohen–Macaulay and B is a smooth A-algebra, then B is Cohen–Macaulay.

Let (R,m,k)→(S,n) be a local map of Noetherian local rings, M a nonzero finite R-module, and N a nonzero finite S-module flat over R. Put S_0=S/mS and N_0=N/mN. Then type_S(M⊗_R N)=type_R(M)·type_{S_0}(N_0), with each type defined by residue-field Ext in the depth degree (equivalently by the socle after a maximal regular sequence). The three modules are nonzero; no Cohen–Macaulay hypothesis is imposed.

A Noetherian local ring R is regular local iff its residue field k has finite projective dimension over R. If R is regular local of dimension d, its global dimension is exactly d (the supremum of projective dimensions of all R-modules, without a finite-generation restriction), and R_p is regular local for every p∈Spec R.

Further-topics scope note: the complete-intersection consequence proved here uses an explicit regular local presentation. Intrinsic complete-intersection characterizations through completions and higher Tor, determinantal-ring Cohen–Macaulayness through determinantal resolutions, and the structure theory of canonical modules require separate theorems and are not additional assertions in this paragraph. References are given for later treatment.

Chapter 8 assumes Noetherian rings throughout, uses depth of a local ring as a module over itself, and tests ring Serre conditions at every prime. Associated-prime and localization facts are recalled from P1-03.
For a Noetherian ring A and an integer j≥0, condition (R_j) means that A_p is regular local for every prime p with ht(p)≤j.
For a Noetherian ring A, a finite A-module M and j≥0, condition (S_j) means depth_{A_p}(M_p)≥min{j, dim Supp_{A_p}(M_p)} for every p∈Supp_A(M). For a ring A the condition uses M=A.
A Noetherian ring A is normal if every prime localization A_p is an integrally closed domain; this includes the zero ring by vacuity.
Q(A), the total quotient ring of a Noetherian ring A, is its localization at the multiplicative set of nonzerodivisors.
Let A be Noetherian and M a finite A-module. For every nonzero x∈M there exists p∈Ass_A(M) such that x/1≠0 in M_p.
For A Noetherian and M finite, M satisfies (S₁) if and only if every associated prime of M is minimal in Supp_A(M).
A Noetherian ring A is reduced if and only if A satisfies (R₀) and (S₁).
For every reduced Noetherian ring A, Q(A) is isomorphic to the finite product ∏_{p minimal} Frac(A/p). For the zero ring this is the empty product.

For a reduced Noetherian ring A, A is normal if and only if it is integrally closed in Q(A). If these conditions hold then A is a finite product of integrally closed domains (allowing the empty product when A=0).
Let A be a Noetherian domain and L a nonzero finitely generated A-submodule of Frac(A). For every u∈Frac(A), if uL⊆L then u is integral over A.

For a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain (A,m), the following are equivalent: A is integrally closed; A is regular local; A is a discrete valuation ring. Under these conditions, for every generator π of m and every z∈Frac(A) with z≠0, there are a unit u∈A× and a unique integer n∈ℤ with z=uπ^n.
If A is a Noetherian integrally closed local domain, then depth A≥min{2,dim A}.
Let A be a Noetherian ring satisfying (S₂). For every z∈Q(A), if its image in Q(A_p) belongs to the image of A_p for every prime p of height at most one, then z belongs to the image of A in Q(A).
Every positive-dimensional Noetherian normal domain A satisfies A=⋂_{ht(p)=1} A_p, the intersection being taken inside Frac(A).
A Noetherian ring is normal if and only if it satisfies (R₁) and (S₂).
A Noetherian ring whose localization at every prime is regular local is normal.
A Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian ring is normal if and only if it is regular at every prime of height at most one.

Let A be a Noetherian normal domain and U⊆Spec(A) an open set containing every prime of height at most one. Every regular function on U is the restriction of a unique element of A; equivalently the restriction map A→Γ(U,𝒪) is bijective.

For any field k, the local cusp ring A=k[t²,t³]_(t²,t³) is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain of depth one. It satisfies (S₂) and fails (R₁), illustrating that (S₂) alone does not imply normality; t∈Frac(A) is integral over A and is not in A.

For any field k, set B=k[x,y]_(x,y), C=k[z,w]_(z,w), and A=B×_k C using the residue maps. This is the localization at the origin of k[x,y,z,w]/(xz,xw,yz,yw). It is a two-dimensional Noetherian local ring of depth one, satisfies (R₁), and fails (S₂), illustrating the independence of the two Serre conditions.
If A is Noetherian, A→B is étale and A is normal, then B is normal.
If A is Noetherian, A→B is faithfully flat and étale, and B is normal, then A is normal.

In the local arguments of Chapter 9, (R,m,k) is a nonzero Noetherian local ring and d=dim R. Finite-module depth and P1-03 homological prerequisites are used. The canonical modules treated here are those for Cohen–Macaulay local rings; separately stated general change-of-rings results retain their stated generality.
For an R-module M over a nonzero Noetherian local ring (R,m,k), Soc_R(M)=0:_M m={x∈M:mx=0}.
For any R-module M over (R,m,k), the socle 0:_M m is naturally isomorphic to Hom_R(k,M).
For a finite nonzero module M over (R,m,k), its type is r_R(M)=dim_k Ext_R^{depth_R M}(k,M). The type of R is r_R(R).
A nonzero Noetherian local ring R is Gorenstein if R has finite injective dimension as an R-module. A Noetherian ring is Gorenstein if every prime localization is a Gorenstein local ring.
For a nonzero Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring R, a canonical module is a finite maximal Cohen–Macaulay R-module of type one and finite injective dimension over R.
Let (R,m,k) be a nonzero Noetherian local ring, N a finite R-module and n≥0. Then injdim_R N≤n if and only if Ext_R^i(k,N)=0 for every integer i>n.
For a finite nonzero module N over a nonzero Noetherian local ring (R,m,k), if its injective dimension is finite, it equals the greatest degree i with Ext_R^i(k,N)≠0.

Let S→R be a homomorphism of commutative unital rings, N an S-module, and c≥0 such that Ext_S^j(R,N)=0 for all cohomological degrees j≠c. Put W=Ext_S^c(R,N) with its natural R-action. For every R-module M and i≥0, there are isomorphisms Ext_R^i(M,W)≅Ext_S^{i+c}(M,N), natural in M, and Ext_S^j(M,N)=0 for j<c. In particular, if R=S/(x) and x is a nonzerodivisor on S and on N, the hypotheses hold with c=1 and W≅N/xN.

Let (R,m,k) be an Artinian local ring and E an injective envelope of k. The functor D=Hom_R(-,E) is an exact contravariant duality on finite R-modules, preserves their lengths, and has the natural evaluation isomorphism M≅D(D(M)) for every finite M. In particular E is finite and ℓ_R(E)=ℓ_R(R).
Every self-injective nonzero Noetherian local ring is Artinian.
An Artinian local ring (R,m,k) is self-injective if and only if dim_k Soc_R(R)=1.
Over a nonzero Noetherian local ring of depth zero, every finite module with finite injective dimension is injective.

For a nonzero Noetherian local ring (R,m,k) of dimension d, the following are equivalent: R is Gorenstein; R is Cohen–Macaulay of type one; Ext_R^i(k,R)=0 for all sufficiently large i. Under these conditions injdim_R R=d, Ext_R^i(k,R)=0 for i≠d, and Ext_R^d(k,R)≅k.
Let (R,m,k) be a nonzero Noetherian local ring and x∈m a nonzerodivisor on R. Then R is Gorenstein if and only if R/(x) is Gorenstein.
Every regular Noetherian local ring is Gorenstein.

A quotient of a Gorenstein Noetherian local ring by a regular sequence contained in its maximal ideal is Gorenstein. Consequently any complete intersection presented as a quotient of a regular local ring by a regular sequence in the maximal ideal is Gorenstein.
If R is a Gorenstein Noetherian local ring and p∈Spec(R), then R_p is Gorenstein.
For a flat local map R→S of nonzero Noetherian local rings, with closed fiber F=S/m_R S, S is Gorenstein if and only if both R and F are Gorenstein.
A nonzero Noetherian local ring R is Gorenstein if and only if its m-adic completion is Gorenstein.
For an étale map A→B of Noetherian rings, Gorensteinness of A implies Gorensteinness of B. If the map is also faithfully flat, Gorensteinness of B implies Gorensteinness of A.

Let S be a Gorenstein Noetherian local ring of dimension s and M a nonzero finite Cohen–Macaulay S-module of support dimension e. Set c=s−e. Then Ext_S^i(M,S)=0 for all i≠c, and D=Ext_S^c(M,S) is a nonzero finite Cohen–Macaulay S-module of dimension e. For every x in the maximal ideal which is regular on M, multiplication by x on D is injective and D/xD≅Ext_S^{c+1}(M/xM,S).

Let S↠R be a surjection from a Gorenstein Noetherian local ring of dimension s to a nonzero Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring of dimension d. The R-module ω_R=Ext_S^{s−d}(R,S), with its natural R-action, is canonical: it is finite maximal Cohen–Macaulay, of type one and finite injective dimension. Precisely, injdim_R ω_R=d, Ext_R^i(k,ω_R)=0 for i≠d and Ext_R^d(k,ω_R)≅k. For every R-module M and i≥0, Ext_R^i(M,ω_R)≅Ext_S^{i+s−d}(M,S).
Let R be a nonzero Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring with canonical module ω. If x is the first element of a system of parameters of positive length, then ω/xω is canonical for R/(x).
Let R be a nonzero Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring with canonical module ω. For every finite maximal Cohen–Macaulay R-module M and every i>0, Ext_R^i(M,ω)=0.

Let R be a nonzero Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring with canonical module ω. The functor D(M)=Hom_R(M,ω) preserves finite maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules, with the zero module adjoined, and is an exact contravariant duality on this category. For every such M, the natural evaluation map M→D(D(M)), m↦(f↦f(m)), is an isomorphism.
For a nonzero Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring R with canonical module ω, the scalar homomorphism R→End_R(ω), r↦(w↦rw), is an isomorphism.
Any two canonical modules of a nonzero Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring are isomorphic, whenever they exist.
If a nonzero Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring R has canonical module ω, then R is Gorenstein if and only if ω≅R as R-modules.

For a nonzero Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring R admitting a Gorenstein local presentation, the isomorphism type of Ext_S^{dim S−dim R}(R,S) is independent of the chosen surjection from a Gorenstein Noetherian local ring S onto R.
For every field k and integer n≥1, the Artinian local ring k[t]/(t^n) has one-dimensional socle spanned by the class of t^{n−1}, and is Gorenstein. The case n=1 is included.

For every field k, the Artinian local ring R=k[x,y]/(x,y)² is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension zero. Its socle is the two-dimensional k-span of the classes of x and y, so R is not Gorenstein. Its canonical module is an injective envelope of its residue field k.
If S is a regular Noetherian local ring and f is a nonzerodivisor in its maximal ideal, then S/(f) is Gorenstein and its canonical module constructed from S is Ext_S¹(S/(f),S)≅S/(f).

The passage to general local duality, local cohomology, normalized dualizing complexes, and additional existence statements is deferred to other tools and treatments; no further theorem is asserted here beyond the finite-length and maximal Cohen–Macaulay dualities already inventoried.

For any commutative ring R and module T, if Ext¹_R(T,V)=0 for every R-module V then T is projective. More generally vanishing of Ext_R^(b+1)(M,V) for every V makes the bth syzygy projective and bounds pd_R M by b.
