For split maximal T of a connected reductive k-group G, Borels containing T correspond to the positive systems of Φ(G,T) and the Weyl group acts simply transitively on these systems. Each such B satisfies B=T⋉R_u(B), and multiplication of the positive root groups in an order gives a scheme parametrization of R_u(B).
For a smooth closed subgroup P of a connected reductive k-group G, G/P is proper if and only if P_bar k contains a Borel.

For a split Borel pair (B,T) with simple roots Δ, a pinning gives an α-equivariant isomorphism x_α:G_a→U_α for every α∈Δ. It is equivalent to a choice of nonzero vector in each simple root line via differentiation at the identity, and a different parametrization changes this vector by nonzero scalar multiplication. The choice of B gives the base of the corresponding based root datum.
A connected reductive group over any field k is quasi-split if it has a k-Borel.

For a split semisimple group the adjoint criterion is X=ℤΦ and the simply connected criterion is Y=ℤΦ∨. The adjoint form and the simply connected central cover have these respective lattices, with the corresponding root and coroot data.

Let f:(G₁,T₁)→(G₂,T₂) be a central isogeny of split connected reductive pairs carrying T₁ onto T₂. Then the pullback X*(T₂)→X*(T₁) is injective of finite index and takes Φ₂ bijectively to Φ₁. The corresponding root-group restrictions of f are isomorphisms and the dual pushforward X_*(T₁)→X_*(T₂) sends the corresponding coroots to one another, including in inseparable characteristic.

Algebraic simple connectedness for a semisimple group means that a central isogeny onto it from a connected semisimple group is an isomorphism, tested geometrically. This tests all central kernels, including nonsmooth ones. The simply connected cover in the split case is obtained from the coroot lattice and its dual, with the same roots and coroots.

For SL₂ take the character generator x(diag(t,t^{-1}))=t, with dual generator y. The positive root and its coroot are 2x and y. For PGL₂ take the ratio x′ of the two diagonal entries with dual y′, giving root x′ and coroot 2y′. The quotient SL₂→PGL₂ pulls x′ back to 2x and pushes y to 2y′. Its scheme kernel is μ₂. In characteristic two that kernel has one-dimensional tangent space, and the derivative sl₂→gl₂/kI is the class map with kernel kI.
For n≥1, the central quotient SL_n→PGL_n has scheme kernel μ_n.

For n≥1 and a field k, every projective class in PGL_n(k) has a representative A∈GL_n(k), and is in the image of SL_n(k) if and only if det A is an n-th power in k×. For n=2 over R a negative determinant class does not lift. This is the obstruction given by its quotient fibre torsor.

Over any field k the groupoid of split pinned connected reductive groups is equivalent via the based root datum to the groupoid of based reduced root data. Every datum is realized and each specified based root-datum isomorphism lifts to exactly one pinning-preserving group isomorphism. After forgetting the pinning, the isomorphism classes of split connected reductive groups are still classified by reduced root data up to isomorphism.

Every based reduced root datum is realized over ℤ by a smooth affine split pinned group of finite presentation with geometrically connected reductive fibres and split fibrewise maximal torus. Its full root and coroot lattices and base in every fibre are those of the given datum.

Two smooth affine groups over ℤ with connected reductive geometric fibres and split fibrewise maximal tori having the same fixed based root datum are isomorphic under that datum identification if it matches their integral pinnings, which specify a basis of each simple root line.

Given split pinned connected reductive k-groups with a basis-compatible root bijection d:Φ₁→Φ₂ and a finite-index injection h:X₂→X₁ as in lines 3461–3469, satisfying h(d(α))=α and h∨(α∨)=d(α)∨ for every root, the prescribed torus map extends to a central isogeny inducing the indicated root-group identifications and matching the simple pins. This holds over any field and gives a pinned isomorphism if h is an isomorphism.
The cited general isogeny theorem with root powers q(α) and Frobenius root maps is mentioned for comparison. The chapter's central lifting result uses power one on every root and coroot.
For a closed subgroup scheme H of G, define G/H to be the fppf sheafification of R↦G(R)/H(R) using right multiplication by H. Its sections are locally represented by cosets gH.
A parabolic subgroup of a connected reductive group is a smooth closed subgroup whose geometric fibre contains a Borel, equivalently one with proper quotient G/P.

For any finite-type affine group scheme G over a field k and any closed subgroup scheme H, the fppf quotient G/H is a quasi-projective k-scheme and q:G→G/H is an fppf right H-torsor. The morphism G×H→G×_{G/H}G given by (g,h)↦(g,gh) is an isomorphism. Formation of the quotient commutes with field extension. If H is smooth, q is smooth. If H is normal, this quotient is the affine group quotient.

For finite-type affine G over k and closed H, the natural map G(k)/H(k)→(G/H)(k) is injective. Define δ(x) to be the fppf H-torsor class of the fibre q^{-1}(x). The image of that injection is the neutral fibre of δ, and the image of δ is exactly the neutral fibre of H¹_fppf(k,H)→H¹_fppf(k,G) given by extension of structure group. These are maps of pointed sets. The fibres of δ are precisely the G(k)-orbits in (G/H)(k).

For k=F_p(t), the fppf quotient G_m/μ_p≃G_m is induced by p-th power. Its fibre over t is a nontrivial μ_p-torsor with no point either over k or over a separable closure, since a p-th root of t is purely inseparable and t is not a p-th power by its t-adic valuation.
For smooth H the fppf classes of H-torsors over the field k are computed by Galois cohomology over the separable closure.

For a split connected reductive pair (G,T) and chosen Borel B⊃T, use its positive roots Φ⁺, U⁺=R_u(B), and U⁻=R_u(B⁻) for the Borel opposite B relative to T, with root system −Φ⁺. The simple reflections fix the length ℓ and longest element w₀ of W(G,T).

In the split connected reductive setting with Borel B containing T, multiplication is an open immersion U⁻×T×U⁺→G with dense image. For any k-rational normalizer representative n_{w₀} of the longest Weyl element, left translation by n_{w₀} identifies that open cell with the open fppf double orbit Bn_{w₀}B.

For GL_n with upper triangular B, the U⁻TU⁺ cell is the open subscheme of invertible matrices with every leading principal minor invertible. On any test algebra the unique lower unitriangular, invertible diagonal, upper unitriangular factorization exists exactly there and gives an inverse morphism. The leading j-th minor is the product of the first j diagonal entries of the diagonal factor.

For split connected reductive G with B⊃T and rational representative n_w of each w∈W, put U_w=U⁺∩n_wU⁻n_w^{-1}. Its ordered root coordinates are the groups for Φ⁺∩wΦ⁻. The locally closed fppf double orbit C(w)=Bn_wB is isomorphic to U_w×B by (u,b)↦un_wb. These double orbits form a pairwise disjoint locally closed stratification of G, their corresponding cells in G/B are A_k^{ℓ(w)}, and their k-points are exactly B(k)n_wB(k).
Each geometric parabolic of a connected reductive group equals its scheme-theoretic normalizer.

For a split connected reductive group with standard Borel B⊃T and simple roots Δ, put Φ_I=Φ∩ℤI for I⊆Δ, and T_I equal to the largest subtorus of ∩_{α∈I}ker α. The standard parabolics containing B are precisely the unique P_I with Bruhat cell indices W_I=⟨s_α:α∈I⟩. Their Levi L_I=Z_G(T_I) has absolute roots Φ_I, and P_I=R_u(P_I)⋊L_I with R_u(P_I) parametrized as a scheme by the ordered product of U_α for α∈Φ⁺∖Φ_I.

For the Weyl group in the split setting, v≤w in Bruhat order if a subword of a reduced simple-reflection expression of w represents v. Equivalently that subword may be required to be reduced, and the criterion is independent of the reduced expression of w.

In a split connected reductive group the reduced closure of C_w=C(w)/B in G/B is the union of the cells C_v for v≤w in Bruhat order. The reduced closure of the double cell C(w) in G has the corresponding union of double cells with the same indices.

For split connected reductive G and a standard parabolic P_I, the B-orbits on G/P_I are indexed by the unique shortest representatives W^I of the cosets wW_I. The orbit of n_wP_I for w∈W^I is isomorphic to A_k^{ℓ(w)}, and its closure is the union of the orbits indexed by v∈W^I with v≤w.
For any parabolic P of a connected reductive k-group G, its homogeneous quotient G/P is smooth and projective over k.

For GL_n the standard parabolic P_I is the stabilizer of the chosen subflag of the coordinate flag E_j=k^j⊂k^n. Its fppf quotient represents flags of the selected dimensions in families, with the flags given by subbundles locally admitting an adapted basis.

For Gr(d,n), 0≤d≤n, the pivot tuples 1≤i₁<⋯<i_d≤n index the cells. The tuple cell consists of planes L with dim(L∩E_j)=#{r:i_r≤j} for every 1≤j≤n. An echelon basis has r-th vector e_{i_r} plus terms in earlier non-pivot positions, giving affine coordinates with ∑_r(i_r−r) free entries. In the reduced closure the equalities become lower bounds imposed by closed rank conditions on L→k^n/E_j. This closure contains exactly the cells with each pivot at most the corresponding i_r, which is precisely Bruhat order on the Grassmannian representatives.

For every connected reductive k-group G over an arbitrary field and every k-parabolic P, there is a k-cocharacter λ with P=P_G(λ). Its geometric unipotent radical descends to U=U_G(λ) and is k-split. It has a k-Levi, given by Z_G(λ) and the product U⋊Z_G(λ). Any two Levi subgroups over k are conjugate by a unique element of U(k). A Levi is a reductive complement to U mapping isomorphically onto P/U.

For a connected reductive k-group G and k-parabolic P, G/P represents parabolics of the geometric type of P. For a test algebra R this means smooth closed parabolic families in G_R whose geometric fibres have the type of P, with the parameter morphism given fppf-locally by gP↦gP_Rg^{-1}.
For every connected reductive k-group G over any field, all minimal k-parabolics are conjugate under G(k) and all maximal k-split tori are conjugate under G(k).
For every connected reductive k-group G over any field and every k-parabolic P, the canonical map G(k)/P(k)→(G/P)(k) is bijective.

For connected reductive G over any k, let S be a maximal k-split torus and P a minimal k-parabolic containing S. Put Z=Z_G(S), N=N_G(S), W_k=N(k)/Z(k). The group scheme N/Z is finite constant with group W_k. For rational representatives n_w of each w∈W_k the disjoint double cosets P(k)n_wP(k) exhaust G(k). The fppf double-orbit schemes Pn_wP are locally closed and pairwise disjoint, but can fail to exhaust G over an algebraic closure.

The relative roots of (G,S), for connected reductive G and maximal k-split S, are the nonzero S-weights in Lie(G). For any maximal k-torus T containing S, they are the nonzero restrictions to S of the absolute roots for T over k_s.

For connected reductive G over any field and maximal k-split torus S every k-parabolic containing S is P_G(λ) for a k-cocharacter of S. Two cocharacters give the same parabolic exactly when the sets of relative roots pairing nonnegatively with them are equal. Those avoiding all relative root hyperplanes give precisely the minimal k-parabolics through S, indexed by the relative chambers, with Levi Z_G(S).

For each relative root a of (G,S), there is a wall reflection r_a in N_G(S)/Z_G(S), represented by a rational normalizer element, and an integral coroot a∨∈X_*(S) characterized by a∨(a(t))=t r_a(t)^{-1} on S. They satisfy r_a(x)=x−⟨x,a∨⟩a and ⟨a,a∨⟩=2. The root–coroot correspondence is equivariant under W_k, the coroots distinguish the roots, and the two lattices with their roots and coroots give a possibly nonreduced relative root datum, including when both a and 2a occur. The reflections generate W_k, which acts simply transitively on relative chambers.

For the real group SU(2,1) of the Hermitian form J with rows (0,0,1),(0,1,0),(1,0,0), the split torus S=diag(t,1,t^{-1}) is maximal. Its relative roots are ±a and ±2a for a(t)=t, of type BC₁. The stabilizer P of the isotropic line C e₁ is a minimal real parabolic. Complexification gives SL₃ with P_C the upper triangular Borel and six absolute cells. The two relative rational double cosets and their orbit schemes are indexed by the identity and the reflection represented by e₁↦e₃, e₂↦−e₂, e₃↦e₁. Their complexifications are exactly the identity and longest-permutation (13) absolute cells, so they omit, for example, the (12) cell.

For a specified split Borel pair T⊂B of a connected split reductive k-group G, take the roots in U=R_u(B) as positive and let Π be the simple roots. On X=X*(T), set μ≤λ when λ−μ is a nonnegative integer combination of Π. A weight λ is dominant if ⟨λ,α∨⟩≥0 for every α∈Π.

For finite-dimensional rational H-modules of an affine k-group scheme H, equivariant Hom spaces and invariant subspaces commute with every extension K/k. If a submodule U₀⊂V has an H_K-equivariant retraction after scalar extension to K, it already has an H-equivariant retraction over k. Consequently semisimplicity descends along all field extensions.

For any affine k-group scheme H with A=O(H), finite-dimensional right A-comodules have rational tensor products, duals, restriction along group homomorphisms, and invariants. The tensor product multiplies the two A-components of the coactions, the dual uses the inverse transpose (the antipode on the transposed coefficient matrix), restriction applies the coordinate Hopf map to the coaction, and invariants are the vectors satisfying δ(v)=v⊗1.

For a finite-dimensional rational module of a connected split reductive group with split Borel pair, a T-weight vector v∈V_μ and any root parametrization x_α:G_a→U_α satisfy the polynomial identity x_α(c)v=v+Σ_{j≥1}c^jv_j, with finitely many nonzero terms and v_j∈V_{μ+jα}. A rational representative n_w∈N_G(T)(k) maps V_μ isomorphically onto V_{wμ}.

A primitive vector is a nonzero T-weight vector fixed by U. It spans a B-stable line on which B acts through B/U=T, and the U-invariants in a rational G-module are T-stable with their corresponding weight decomposition.

For a finite-dimensional rational G-module generated by a primitive vector v_λ, its weight-λ space is kv_λ, all other weights are strictly less than λ in the simple-root order, and λ is dominant. The sum of all proper G-submodules is the unique maximal proper G-submodule.
Each simple rational module of the connected split reductive group G has a unique primitive line. Two simple rational G-modules with the same highest weight are isomorphic.

For λ∈X*(T), use the B⁻-module k_λ from the character extended through B⁻→T, and construct the G-equivariant line bundle L_λ=G×^{B⁻}k_λ over the right quotient Y=G/B⁻ with (g,z)b=(gb,λ(b)⁻¹z). Identify ∇(λ)=H⁰(Y,L_λ) with the regular functions f on G satisfying f(gb)=λ(b)⁻¹f(g). It is a finite-dimensional rational G-module for (hf)(g)=f(h⁻¹g).
For a finite-dimensional rational G-module V and λ∈X*(T), evaluation at 1 induces the isomorphism Hom_G(V,∇(λ)) ≃ Hom_{B⁻}(V,k_λ).

For a central isogeny π:G′→G of connected split reductive k-groups and the opposite Borel B′⁻ above B⁻, the scheme inverse image is B′⁻, mapping faithfully flat onto B⁻. The induced morphism of fppf quotients G′/B′⁻→G/B⁻ is an isomorphism under which L_{π*λ} is the pullback of L_λ for every actual character λ. This includes nonsmooth kernels.

The induced module ∇(λ) is nonzero if and only if λ∈X*(T) is dominant. When nonzero it has a simple socle that is its unique simple submodule and its primitive line has weight λ. Writing w₀ for the longest Weyl element, every weight μ satisfies w₀λ≤μ≤λ.
For a split connected semisimple group G, its character lattice is the full weight lattice if and only if G is simply connected.

For each dominant weight λ in the actual lattice X*(T), let L(λ) be the simple socle of ∇(λ). These modules classify all simple rational G-modules over k, with λ their highest weight. End_G(L(λ))=k and for every field extension the base-changed module remains simple with highest weight λ.

For SL₂ with t↦diag(t,t⁻¹), the weight group is Z, its positive root is 2, and its dominant weights are m≥0. Pullback from PGL₂ gives the sublattice 2Z. The scheme centre μ₂ acts on L(m) by z↦z^m, so L(m) descends along SL₂→PGL₂ exactly when m is even. In characteristic 2 the odd-exponent character is still nontrivial on the coordinate Hopf algebra although μ₂(k̄) is trivial.

A connected affine algebraic group H in characteristic zero is reductive if and only if every finite-dimensional rational H-representation is semisimple, or equivalently if and only if some faithful finite-dimensional rational H-representation is semisimple.
For a dominant weight λ, set λ*=−w₀λ and define the Weyl module Δ(λ)=∇(λ*)∨.

For each dominant λ, ∇(λ) has socle L(λ) and Δ(λ) has head L(λ). The highest-weight spaces of Δ(λ), L(λ) and ∇(λ) are all one-dimensional. The simple dual is L(λ)∨≃L(−w₀λ). In characteristic zero all three modules are isomorphic.
For a finite-dimensional rational G-module V, its formal T-character is ch_T(V)=Σ_{μ∈X*(T)} dim_k(V_μ)e^μ in the integral group ring Z[X*(T)].
The formal T-character is additive in short exact sequences and multiplicative under tensor products. Restriction to T induces an isomorphism of rings K₀(Rep_k G)≃Z[X*(T)]^W.
Let ρ=½Σ_{α∈Φ⁺}α and set A(e^ν)=Σ_{w∈W}(−1)^{ℓ(w)}e^{wν}. Interpret the expressions in Z[½X] when ρ is outside the actual character lattice X.

Pullback along a central isogeny injects the character lattices and preserves the Weyl group and the root correspondence. This allows a character identity to be checked on such a cover, including one where ρ is integral.

In characteristic p>0 the Frobenius kernel G_r is ker(F_G^r) for the iterated relative Frobenius. For a finite group scheme K define Dist(K)=k[K]∨ with product dual to the Hopf coproduct. Its modules are equivalent to the representations of K via pairing of the coaction with the dual algebra.

Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, let G be connected split reductive, q=p^r and G_r=ker(F_G^r). For dominant η with 0≤⟨η,α∨⟩<q at every simple root, the simple rational G-module L(η) remains simple on G_r.
Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, for a simply connected semisimple G, q=p^r, ρ the half-sum of the positive roots and N=|Φ⁺|, the simple module L((q−1)ρ) has dimension q^N.

For every λ∈X*(T), the equivariant Euler characteristic of L_λ on Y=G/B⁻ is Σ_{i≥0}(−1)^i ch_T H^i(Y,L_λ)=A(e^{λ+ρ})/A(e^ρ), interpreted in the fraction ring of the character group ring enlarged to the half-lattice if needed, or equivalently after multiplication by the denominator.
For every dominant λ∈X*(T), H^i(G/B⁻,L_λ)=0 for every i>0 and every characteristic.

For the positive roots of the split connected reductive pair with ρ their half sum and A the Weyl alternant, the Weyl denominator is A(e^ρ)=e^ρ∏_{α∈Φ⁺}(1−e^{−α}), interpreted in the integral group ring of the half-lattice when necessary.

For any dominant λ, in every characteristic, the induced and Weyl modules have equal formal character A(e^{λ+ρ})/A(e^ρ). This also gives the character of L(λ) when the induced module is simple, in particular in characteristic zero.

For any dominant λ, in every characteristic, the common dimension of ∇(λ) and Δ(λ) is Π_{α∈Φ⁺}⟨λ+ρ,α∨⟩/⟨ρ,α∨⟩, with the empty product equal to 1. This is also the dimension of L(λ) when the induced module is simple, in particular in characteristic zero.

For SL₂ and m≥0, the Weyl character quotient is e^m+e^{m−2}+⋯+e^{−m} and the induced module ∇(m) has dimension m+1 in every characteristic. In characteristic p the example m=p has simple socle of dimension 2 although ∇(p) has dimension p+1.

For n≥1 and upper triangular Borel, the dominant weights of GL_n are precisely integer n-tuples λ₁≥⋯≥λ_n. For each finite-dimensional rational representation some twist by det^a with integer a≥0 is polynomial. The simple module L(λ) is polynomial precisely when λ_n≥0. Scalar matrices act on L(λ) with degree Σ_iλ_i, and on the central degree-d summand of a polynomial representation the coefficient polynomials are homogeneous of degree d.

For GL_n, a rational representation is polynomial when its matrix coefficient functions lie in k[x_{ij}] inside k[x_{ij},det⁻¹]. The central degree-d summand is the weight space on which the scalar torus acts by z↦z^d.

The dual of the defining GL_n-module has highest weight (0,…,0,−1), with the single coordinate −1 for n=1, and twisting by det makes its coefficients the matrix cofactors with the appropriate indices.

Over any ground field, homogeneous polynomial simple GL_n-modules of degree d are indexed by the partitions of d of length at most n. Over ℂ this indexing matches that of the multiplicity modules in the cited Schur–Weyl decomposition. In positive characteristic a homogeneous polynomial representation can fail to be semisimple, as in the symmetric-power example.
In characteristic p>0 a pullback along relative Frobenius can be a nontrivial rational representation with zero differential.

For a connected semisimple group H over a characteristic-zero field, differentiation from finite-dimensional rational H-modules to finite-dimensional modules of Lie(H) is fully faithful. If H is simply connected it is essentially surjective. If H is split, a simple Lie algebra module integrates precisely when its highest weight belongs to the actual group character lattice.

For SL₂ in characteristic p>0, the pullback of the natural module of the split target along relative Frobenius is nontrivial with torus characters p and −p but zero differential, including over finite fields.

In characteristic p>0, Sym^p(k²) for SL₂ is ∇(p), of dimension p+1. Its subspace S=kx^p+ky^p is the Frobenius pullback of the natural module. It is the simple socle L(p), has dimension 2, and has no SL₂-equivariant complement, including p=2.

Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0, for G connected semisimple and simply connected, every dominant weight λ has a unique finite expansion λ=Σ_{i≥0}p^iλ_i with dominant digits satisfying 0≤⟨λ_i,α∨⟩

For finite Galois K/k, write Γ=Gal(K/k). A semilinear action on a K-space V consists of additive action maps s_σ with s_σ(av)=σ(a)s_σ(v) and s_{στ}=s_σs_τ. For the separable closure k_s write Γ_k=Gal(k_s/k) with its Krull topology.

For any finite Galois extension K/k and K-vector space V with semilinear Gal(K/k)-action, without dimension bound, the canonical map K⊗_k V^Γ→V, a⊗v↦av, is an isomorphism. Equivariant K-linear maps correspond to k-linear maps on fixed spaces. Fixed spaces and extension yield an equivalence preserving tensor products and the tensor unit. For finite-dimensional V, dim_k V^Γ=dim_K V.

For an affine K-group with semilinear descent data for finite Galois K/k, its Hopf algebra A descends to A^Γ with its multiplication, unit, coproduct, counit, and antipode. Equivariant morphisms descend uniquely, finite type and smoothness descend, and Γ-stable Hopf ideals correspond to closed subgroup schemes of the descended group.

For a group M with the discrete topology and a continuous Γ_k-action, a continuous cocycle a satisfies a(στ)=a(σ)·σ(a(τ)). Identify cocycles by a′(σ)=b⁻¹·a(σ)·σ(b). The quotient H¹(Γ_k,M) is pointed by the constant identity cocycle. For a smooth k-group H, put H¹(k,H)=H¹(Γ_k,H(k_s)).

For any finite-type affine k-group G₀ and finite Galois K/k, k-isomorphism classes of forms split by K (becoming isomorphic to (G₀)_K) are classified by H¹(Gal(K/k),Aut_K((G₀)_K)) with its standard Galois action. Forms becoming isomorphic over k_s are classified by the analogous continuous H¹ with discrete automorphism coefficients.

A right H-torsor becomes isomorphic to H with its right translation action after an fppf base change. Over a field and for an affine group, use the stated criterion that X be nonempty and of finite type and (x,h)↦(x,xh) give an isomorphism X×H→X×X.
For n≥1 both H¹(k,GL_n) and H¹(k,SL_n) are singletons, as are the finite Galois cohomology sets H¹(Gal(K/k),GL_n(K)) and H¹(Gal(K/k),SL_n(K)).
For every smooth affine finite-type k-group H, H¹(k,H) classifies isomorphism classes of fppf right H-torsors. The trivial class is precisely a torsor with a k-point.
In characteristic p, for a∈k outside k^p, the equation x^p=a with the multiplication action of μ_p is an fppf μ_p-torsor with no k_s-point.

For finite Galois K/k and n≥1, central simple k-algebras A of degree n split by K are classified up to algebra isomorphism by H¹(Gal(K/k),PGL_n(K)). Twisting SL_n and PGL_n by the corresponding conjugation cocycle gives SL₁(A), the reduced-norm-one group, and PGL₁(A), the fppf quotient of the units by scalars. These classes retain inner twisting data which may be lost by passing to group isomorphism classes.

For n≥3 transpose-inverse gives an outer symmetry in type A. Inversion into the opposite algebra induces a group isomorphism SL₁(A)→SL₁(A^op), illustrating loss of the inner twisting data at the level of abstract group-scheme isomorphism classes.

For a split connected reductive k-group G₀ with pinned based root datum Ψ⁺, the fppf automorphism sequence has kernel (G₀)_ad and quotient the constant étale group Aut(Ψ⁺), and splits by the pinning. A form has the twisted outer sheaf and the corresponding adjoint kernel.
Two forms of G₀ represented in H¹(k,Aut(G₀)) are inner forms of each other exactly when their images in H¹(k,Aut(Ψ⁺)) coincide. Each resulting fiber has exactly one quasi-split isomorphism class.

For a separable quadratic extension K/k, T=ker(N:Res_{K/k} G_m→G_m) is a k-torus with X*(T_K)=Z and its nonidentity Galois element acting by negation. Canonically H¹(k,T)≃k^×/N_{K/k}(K^×). For C/R this group has order two.
For a finite separable field extension E/k, the Galois cohomology pointed set H¹(k,Res_{E/k} G_m) is a singleton.
For a smooth connected finite-type group scheme G over F_q, the map L:g↦F(g)g⁻¹ on geometric points is surjective for the q-power Frobenius endomorphism F over F_q, and the fiber at L(g) is gG(F_q).

For a connected finite-type group scheme G over F_q, any nonempty finite-type F_q-scheme X on whose geometric points G acts transitively has an F_q-point. In particular a torsor under such a connected group is trivial.

For a smooth affine k-group G and a smooth closed subgroup H, the sequence G(k)→(G/H)(k)→H¹(k,H)→H¹(k,G) is exact at the indicated base points. Two rational points of the right quotient G/H have the same H¹(k,H)-class if and only if they lie in the same G(k)-orbit. If k is finite and H connected, every rational point of G/H lifts to G(k).
Over a finite field, every smooth connected affine group has a k-Borel subgroup and a geometrically maximal k-torus. In particular every connected reductive group over a finite field is quasi-split.
Over F_q for odd q, the quotient map G_m→G_m, t↦t², with disconnected kernel μ₂ does not lift a nonsquare rational point.
The norm-one torus of a separable quadratic field extension has geometric rank one and k-rank zero.

For a connected semisimple k-group, positive k-rank is equivalent to the existence of a proper k-parabolic. For a connected reductive k-group, the same proper-parabolic criterion uses positive k-rank of the adjoint quotient G_ad.
For a connected reductive k-group, its k-rank is the dimension of a maximal k-split torus. In the split case this equals the geometric rank.

For a connected reductive k-group the k-rank is independent of the chosen maximal k-split torus and is at most the geometric rank. For a connected semisimple group the k-ranks of G and its adjoint quotient coincide.

For an affine algebraic Q-group G and a closed faithful matrix realization i:G↪GL_N, the commensurability class in G(Q) of i⁻¹(GL_N(Z)) is independent of i. The same holds in G(K) for a number field K and a fixed ring O_{K,S} of S-integers for finite S containing the infinite places.
SL_n(Z) and its principal congruence subgroups, the kernels of reduction, are arithmetic subgroups of SL_n(Q), and embed in SL_n(R). The Q-rank of SL_n is n−1.

An arithmetic subgroup over Q is a subgroup of G(Q) in the commensurability class of the integral-point subgroup from a closed faithful matrix realization. The term lattice in G(R) also requires finite covolume.

For every connected absolutely almost simple group G over a global field K (number field or global function field), and every finite nonempty set S of its places, the diagonal image of G(K) is dense in the restricted product outside S if and only if G is algebraically simply connected and Π_{v∈S}G(K_v) is noncompact.

For a number field K, finite set of places S and closed matrix realization G↪GL_N, define G(O_v)=G(K_v)∩GL_N(O_v) at each finite place. These are compact open subgroups. The S-adelic group is the restricted product of G(K_v), v∉S, relative to those subgroups, with ordinary topology on archimedean factors outside S. Basic opens prescribe ordinary opens at the archimedean factors and at finitely many finite places, and the prescribed compact open subgroups at the other outside places. This group topology is independent of the closed realization and the diagonal map G(K)→G(A_K^S) is a well-defined group homomorphism.

Weak approximation at a finite set of places concerns density of the rational diagonal in the ordinary product over those places. Strong approximation outside S concerns density in the restricted product of all outside places, whose basic opens also impose the stipulated integrality conditions at the remaining finite places.
For SL_n/Q with n≥2, the real group is noncompact and the diagonal image of SL_n(Q) in the restricted product of all finite SL_n(Q_p) is dense, i.e. strong approximation holds outside S={∞}.

PGL₂/Q has a noncompact real group but fails strong approximation outside {∞}. In the integral model from conjugation on M₂, the nonempty adelic open prescribing integral invertible representatives at all finite places and a nonsquare unit determinant class at 5 has no point of PGL₂(Q). For example the local class of diag(2,1) at 5 and identity classes elsewhere lies in this open.

For the global fields, group, and finite nonempty set S of the strong approximation criterion, if the inside product Π_{v∈S}G(K_v) is compact, the diagonal projection outside S is closed and discrete. For a positive-dimensional smooth group the outside local group is nondiscrete, so strong approximation fails.

For a central division algebra D over a global field K and m≥2, the reduced-norm-one group SL_m(D)=SL₁(M_m(D)) satisfies strong approximation outside every finite nonempty set S. Its groups of local points are noncompact at all places, including when the group is nonsplit.
Bibliography and TeX back matter identifying references for the preceding chapters.

For a connected semisimple group over a number field at a finite set of places, the closure of the rational diagonal in the local product contains an identity neighborhood and the embedded archimedean identity components. In the globally anisotropic case the closure has finite index and contains the embedded subgroups generated by the radicals of rational parabolics at each isotropic finite factor.
A connected semisimple group over a number field with no positive-dimensional rational split torus has compact quotient of its full adelic group by the diagonal rational points.
Over each completion of a number field, the local points of a semisimple group are compact exactly when the group is anisotropic.
The strong approximation sufficiency statement applies to every form of type F₄ over a global field, including anisotropic global forms over number fields and all forms over global function fields.
Over a nonarchimedean local field, a homogeneous cubic form in more than nine variables has a nonzero zero.
For every finite extension of a rational function field over a finite field, a homogeneous degree-d form, d ≥ 1, in more than d² variables has a nonzero zero.
Every connected semisimple group of absolute type F₄ over a nonarchimedean local field or a global function field is split.

The stabilizer of a linear subspace can be tested on a basis adapted to the subspace by the vanishing of the off-block entries of each matrix and of its inverse on every test algebra. Geometric point equalities detect the relevant equalities and closed conditions for geometrically reduced sources.
The largest split subgroup of a smooth connected unipotent group can grow after purely inseparable extension, as in the wound plane subgroup of B09.
A connected semisimple group over k and its adjoint quotient by the full scheme centre have equal relative k-ranks.
The rational diagonal of SL_n for n at least 2 satisfies strong approximation away from the real place, and its real group is noncompact.
Compactness of the product at the omitted places makes the outside diagonal image closed and discrete and obstructs strong approximation for the stated positive-dimensional smooth group.
TeX setup, title, contents and overview of the chapter structure and overall mathematical scope.

Standing conventions: rings are commutative with identity, finite modules are finitely generated, the cohomological shift satisfies H^q(K[s]) = H^{q+s}(K), hats for local rings denote maximal-ideal-adic completion, and E_R(k) denotes the injective envelope of the residue field. The passage also explains references and excludes wider literature discussion as an additional theorem scope.

Standing hypotheses in Chapter 1: R is Noetherian, I is an ideal, modules are arbitrary unless explicitly restricted, and connecting homomorphisms have the cochain long-exact-sequence sign. Module localization and exactness are cited prerequisites.
For a Noetherian ring R, ideal I and arbitrary R-module M, define the I-power torsion submodule Γ_I(M) = ⋃_{n≥1}(0:_M I^n), with maps induced by restriction of module homomorphisms.
For a Noetherian ring R and ideal I, Γ_I is an additive left exact functor on all R-modules, determined functorially by √I. Γ_0 is the identity and Γ_R is zero.
For a Noetherian ring R and ideal I, define H_I^q = R^qΓ_I for q≥0 and H_I^q = 0 for q<0.
For a Noetherian ring R and ideal I, every short exact sequence of arbitrary R-modules induces a natural long exact sequence of the H_I^q, with the cochain connecting maps.

For a Noetherian ring R, ideal I, arbitrary R-module M and q≥0, H_I^q(M) ≅ colim_{n≥1} Ext_R^q(R/I^n,M) naturally. The transitions are induced contravariantly by the quotient maps R/I^{n+1} → R/I^n, and the comparison is natural in M and compatible with the maps for short exact sequences.
For a Noetherian ring R, ideal I and arbitrary R-module M, every H_I^q(M) is I-power torsion, meaning that each element is annihilated by some I^n.
For a Noetherian ring R, ideal I and injective R-module Q, the submodule Γ_I(Q) is injective over R.
For any f in a Noetherian ring R and injective R-module Q, the localization map Q → Q_f is surjective with kernel Γ_(f)(Q), including f=0 and units.

For generators f_1,…,f_r of an ideal I of a Noetherian ring R, form the augmented Čech cochain complex C_I^• = ⊗_{j=1}^r [R → R_{f_j}], where each factor has degrees 0 and 1 and the empty tensor is R[0]. In degree q it is the sum of R localized at ∏_{j∈J} f_j over q-element index subsets J, with differential inserting a∉J by localization and the sign (−1)^{#{j∈J:j<a}}.

With the indicated augmented Čech complex for any generators of I in a Noetherian ring R, there is a natural derived comparison C_I^• ⊗_R K ≃ RΓ_I(K) for every bounded-below complex K of R-modules. In particular H_I^q(M) ≅ H^q(C_I^• ⊗_R M) naturally for arbitrary R-modules M.

Over a Noetherian ring the local cohomology calculation is independent of the chosen generators and depends only on √I. If √I = √(g_1,…,g_s), then H_I^q(M)=0 for q>s for any R-module M. For I=0 it equals M in degree zero and is zero in all other degrees, and for I=R it is zero in every degree. In the derived category the zero-ideal derived torsion functor is the identity and the unit-ideal derived torsion functor is zero.

For I=(f_1,…,f_r) in a Noetherian ring and arbitrary R-module M, take the filtered tower of cochain Koszul complexes on f_1^n,…,f_r^n with coefficients in M. The transition n→n+1 in the component indexed by J is multiplication by ∏_{j∈J} f_j (the empty product is 1). Its filtered colimit as a complex is C_I^• ⊗_R M.
For I=(f_1,…,f_r) over a Noetherian ring R and arbitrary R-module M, H_I^r(M) ≅ colim_n M/(f_1^n,…,f_r^n)M with transition multiplication by f_1⋯f_r.
For a homomorphism R→B of Noetherian rings, an ideal I of R and an arbitrary B-module N, H_I^q(N) ≅ H_{IB}^q(N) with compatible B-action, where the left side uses restriction of scalars to R.
If the homomorphism R→B of Noetherian rings is flat, then for every ideal I of R and R-module M, B⊗_R H_I^q(M) ≅ H_{IB}^q(B⊗_R M).
For a Noetherian ring R, ideal I and arbitrary R-module M, Supp H_I^q(M) ⊆ V(I) ∩ Supp M for every q.

For a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) and an 𝔪-power torsion R-module T, the R-action extends uniquely to the 𝔪-adic completion R̂, and the action map R̂⊗_R T → T is an isomorphism. For an element killed by 𝔪^n, the completed scalar acts by its class via R̂/𝔪^nR̂ ≅ R/𝔪^n.
For a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪), any R-module M and every q, H_𝔪^q(M), with its unique extended scalar action, identifies with H_{𝔪R̂}^q(R̂⊗_R M) as an R̂-module.

For a Noetherian ring R, an ideal I, an arbitrary R-module M and U=Spec R ∖ V(I), there is a natural exact sequence 0 → H_I^0(M) → M → Γ(U,M̃) → H_I^1(M) → 0 whose middle map is restriction, and a natural isomorphism H^q(U,M̃) ≅ H_I^{q+1}(M) for q≥1.

For a Noetherian ring R, ideal I and arbitrary R-module M, put X=Spec R and U=X ∖ V(I). The augmented Čech complex C_I^• ⊗_R M naturally identifies in the derived category with the fibre of the derived restriction map RΓ(X,M̃) → RΓ(U,M̃). Equivalently, for a flasque resolution F^• of M̃ the model is the shifted cone Cone(Γ(X,F^•) → Γ(U,F^•))[-1].

For a Noetherian ring R, ideals I,J and an arbitrary R-module M, there is a natural long exact Mayer–Vietoris sequence ⋯ → H_{I+J}^q(M) → H_I^q(M)⊕H_J^q(M) → H_{I∩J}^q(M) → H_{I+J}^{q+1}(M) → ⋯. The maps use diagonal and difference in the augmented restriction sequence.

In Chapter 2, M is finite over a Noetherian ring R. The dimension of M is the Krull dimension of Supp M, with dim 0 = −∞. For an ideal I with V(I)∩Supp M nonempty, grade(I,M) is the length of a maximal M-regular sequence in I; for a disjoint intersection it is +∞.
For a Noetherian ring R, ideal I and finite R-module M, grade(I,M) = inf {q≥0 : H_I^q(M)≠0}, where the infimum of the empty set is +∞.
For a Noetherian ring R, ideal I and a finite R-module M with finite-dimensional support, H_I^q(M)=0 for q>dim M. The zero module uses the convention dim 0=−∞.

Let S be regular local of dimension d with maximal ideal 𝔫 minimally generated by x_1,…,x_d. The Čech fraction class of 1/(x_1⋯x_d) in H_𝔫^d(S) is nonzero, including the empty-product class 1 for d=0.
Let S be regular local of dimension d with maximal ideal 𝔫 minimally generated by x_1,…,x_d. Then every nonzero c∈S acts surjectively on H_𝔫^d(S).
For a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) and nonzero finite R-module M, its completion M̂ has the same support dimension and local depth as M. For every q, H_𝔪^q(M) identifies with H_{𝔪R̂}^q(M̂).
If B is a complete Noetherian local domain of dimension d with maximal ideal 𝔪_B and N is finite over B with positive rank over Frac(B), then H_{𝔪_B}^d(N)≠0.
For a nonzero finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪), H_𝔪^{dim M}(M)≠0.
A nonzero finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if H_𝔪^q(M) vanishes for every q≠dim M. The group H_𝔪^{dim M}(M) is nonzero.
For a Noetherian ring R, an ideal I, a finite R-module M and U=Spec R ∖ V(I), the restriction M → Γ(U,M̃) is an isomorphism if and only if grade(I,M)≥2, including the grade +∞ case.

For a Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\), write \(\widehat R=\varprojlim_n R/\mathfrak m^n\) and \(\operatorname{soc}X=(0:_X\mathfrak m)\) for the \(k\)-vector-space socle of an \(R\)-module \(X\). Finite means finitely generated. An inclusion is essential if its image has nonzero intersection with every nonzero submodule of its target.

For any \(R\)-module \(X\) over a Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\) with residue-field injective hull \(E_R(k)\), the Matlis dual is the contravariant functor \(X^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,E_R(k))\). The \(R\)-action given by multiplying in the target agrees with precomposition by scalar multiplication on \(X\).
Bibliographic references for the organization of the Matlis duality chapter.

For every Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\) there exists an injective hull \(k\hookrightarrow E=E_R(k)\) of its residue field, with essential inclusion and socle equal to the image of \(k\).

For every Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\), the residue-field Matlis dual \(X\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,E_R(k))\) is exact contravariantly on all \(R\)-modules and detects nonzero objects.

For the residue-field injective hull \(E\) of a Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\), set \(E[n]=(0:_E\mathfrak m^n)\) for \(n\ge1\). One has \(E=\bigcup_{n\ge1}E[n]\), and \(k\hookrightarrow E[n]\) is the injective hull of \(k\) over \(R/\mathfrak m^n\).
For any finite-length \(R\)-module \(X\) over a Noetherian local ring, \(X^\vee\) has the same length and the natural evaluation map \(X\to X^{\vee\vee}\) is an isomorphism.

For the residue-field injective hull \(E\) of a Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\), scalar multiplication induces an \(R\)-algebra isomorphism \(\widehat R\simeq\operatorname{End}_R(E)\). For every \(n\ge1\), restricting the scalar endomorphism to \(E[n]\) agrees with multiplication by its reduction in \(R/\mathfrak m^n\).
The injective hull \(E_R(k)\) of the residue field of a Noetherian local ring is Artinian as an \(R\)-module.

Over any Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\), an \(\mathfrak m\)-power-torsion module is Artinian if and only if its socle is finite-dimensional over \(k\). Every Artinian \(R\)-module is \(\mathfrak m\)-power torsion.

If \(R\) is complete Noetherian local, Matlis duality is a contravariant equivalence of the categories of finitely generated and Artinian \(R\)-modules, with the canonical natural evaluation \(X\to X^{\vee\vee}\) an isomorphism on both categories.

For an arbitrary Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\), there is a contravariant Matlis dual equivalence between Artinian \(R\)-modules and finite \(\widehat R\)-modules. From Artinian modules one applies \(\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,E_R(k))\) with the completed action from \(E_R(k)\). From finite \(\widehat R\)-modules one dualizes over \(\widehat R\) into \(E_{\widehat R}(k)\) and restricts scalars to \(R\).

For every finite \(R\)-module \(X\) over an arbitrary Noetherian local ring, there is a natural identification \(X^{\vee\vee}\simeq\widehat X\) carrying the evaluation map \(X\to X^{\vee\vee}\) to the completion map.

Over a Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\), every \(R\)-module \(X\) admits an injective resolution obtained by beginning at \(X\), successively taking the injective hull of each cosyzygy, and taking the cokernel of that essential inclusion as the next cosyzygy. Applying \(\operatorname{Hom}_R(k,-)\) gives zero differentials.
If an injective module \(J\) over a Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\) has \(\dim_k\operatorname{soc}J=t<\infty\), then \(\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}J\simeq E_R(k)^t\), also for \(t=0\).

For every finite \(R\)-module \(X\) over a Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\) and every degree \(i\), \(H^i_{\mathfrak m}(X)\) is Artinian and its Matlis dual is a finite \(\widehat R\)-module.
For cochain complexes the shift convention is \(K[a]^j=K^{j+a}\) and \(d_{K[a]}=(-1)^a d_K\). An unshifted module stands for the complex concentrated in degree zero.
For cochain complexes \(X,Y\), the Hom complex has \(\mathcal H om(X,Y)^a=\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(X^j,Y^{j+a})\) with differential \(d(f)=d_Y f-(-1)^a f d_X\) on degree-\(a\) elements.
The notation \(C_{\mathfrak m}\) invokes the augmented Čech complex from L05, with the ring in degree zero.
Set \(\operatorname{Ext}^j=0\) for negative degrees when both arguments are modules.
Bibliographic references for the local duality formulas.

If \((S,\mathfrak n,k)\) is a Gorenstein local ring of dimension \(n\), there is an isomorphism \(R\Gamma_{\mathfrak n}(S)\simeq E_S(k)[-n]\) in the derived category, with the residue-field injective hull in cohomological degree \(n\).

For a Gorenstein local ring \((S,\mathfrak n,k)\) of dimension \(n\), a finite \(S\)-module \(X\), and a bounded-above degreewise finite free resolution \(P\to X\), there are quasi-isomorphism comparisons \(P\otimes_S C_{\mathfrak n}\simeq X\otimes_S C_{\mathfrak n}\) and \(P\otimes_S C_{\mathfrak n}\simeq P\otimes_S E_S(k)[-n]\).

For a Gorenstein local ring \((S,\mathfrak n,k)\) of dimension \(n\), finite \(S\)-module \(X\), bounded-above degreewise finite free resolution \(P\to X\), and \(E_S=E_S(k)\), the dual \(\mathcal H om_S(P\otimes_S E_S[-n],E_S[0])\) is identified by tensor–Hom adjunction with \(\mathcal H om_S(P,\widehat S[n])\). Here scalar multiplication identifies the inner endomorphism module \(\operatorname{End}_S(E_S)\) with \(\widehat S\).

Let \((S,\mathfrak n,k)\) be a Gorenstein local ring of dimension \(n\). For every finite \(S\)-module \(X\) and degree \(i\), there are isomorphisms natural in \(X\) and linear over \(\widehat S\), \((H^i_{\mathfrak n}(X))^\vee\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{n-i}_S(X,\widehat S) \cong\widehat{\operatorname{Ext}^{n-i}_S(X,S)}\).

For a surjective local map \(S\twoheadrightarrow R\) between Noetherian local rings with residue field \(k\) and maximal ideals \(\mathfrak n\) and \(\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n R\), the \(R\)-linear identification \(E_R(k)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(R,E_S(k))\) uses the action by precomposing with multiplication on \(R\).

For a surjective local map \(S\twoheadrightarrow R\) of Noetherian local rings with residue field \(k\) and \(\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n R\), the local cohomology of any \(R\)-module \(X\) over \(R\) is computed by the augmented Čech model over \(S\) applied to \(X\), and there is the adjunction \(\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,\operatorname{Hom}_S(R,E_S(k))) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_S(X,E_S(k))\). Both comparisons respect the \(R\)-action.

For every complete Noetherian local ring \(R\) with residue field \(k\) and every complete regular local cover \(S\twoheadrightarrow R\) as in C04 of dimension \(n\), define \(\mathcal D_R=\operatorname{RHom}_S(R,S[n])\) with its \(R\)-action on the argument \(R\). It is represented by a bounded complex of injective \(R\)-modules and has finitely generated cohomology modules.

For \(\mathcal D_R=\operatorname{RHom}_S(R,S[n])\) of a complete Noetherian local \(R\) and a complete regular local cover of dimension \(n\), the actual scalar homothety morphism \(R\to\operatorname{RHom}_R(\mathcal D_R,\mathcal D_R)\) is an isomorphism, and \(\operatorname{RHom}_R(k,\mathcal D_R)\simeq k[0]\) for the residue field \(k\).

For every complete Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\), finite \(R\)-module \(X\), and degree \(i\), there is an \(R\)-linear isomorphism \((H^i_{\mathfrak m}(X))^\vee \cong H^{-i}(\operatorname{RHom}_R(X,\mathcal D_R))\) natural in \(X\).

For every complete Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\), with a chosen \(E_R(k)\), the complex \(\mathcal H om_R(C_{\mathfrak m},E_R(k)[0])\) represents the normalized dualizing complex \(\mathcal D_R\). The comparison applies for any finite generating list of the maximal ideal.

For every Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\), every finite \(R\)-module \(X\), and every degree \(i\), there is an isomorphism of \(\widehat R\)-modules \((H^i_{\mathfrak m}(X))^\vee\cong H^{-i}(\operatorname{RHom}_{\widehat R}(\widehat X,\mathcal D_{\widehat R}))\).

For a complete Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\) of dimension \(d\), the canonical module is \(\omega_R=H^{-d}(\mathcal D_R)\). It is finite, is isomorphic to \((H^d_{\mathfrak m}(R))^\vee\), and has \(\omega_R^\vee\cong H^d_{\mathfrak m}(R)\). It is the unique finite \(R\)-module up to isomorphism with this latter dual.

A complete Noetherian local ring \(R\) of dimension \(d\) is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if \(\mathcal D_R\simeq\omega_R[d]\). In that case, for a complete regular local cover \(S\twoheadrightarrow R\) of dimension \(n\), its canonical module is \(\omega_R\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{n-d}_S(R,S)\) with the natural quotient-ring action.

For a complete Cohen–Macaulay local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\) of dimension \(d\), a finite \(R\)-module \(X\), and every \(i\), the identifications \((H^i_{\mathfrak m}(X))^\vee\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{d-i}_R(X,\omega_R)\) and \(H^i_{\mathfrak m}(X)\cong (\operatorname{Ext}^{d-i}_R(X,\omega_R))^\vee\) are natural in \(X\).

For a noncomplete Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\) of dimension \(d\), a finite \(R\)-module \(X\), and every \(i\), the analogous two comparisons identify the Matlis dual of \(H^i_{\mathfrak m}(X)\) with \(\operatorname{Ext}^{d-i}_{\widehat R}(\widehat X,\omega_{\widehat R})\) and \(H^i_{\mathfrak m}(X)\) with the Matlis dual of that Ext module over the completed ring, using the completion identifications. If a finite \(R\)-module \(\omega\) with \(\widehat\omega\simeq\omega_{\widehat R}\) is given, the dual of \(H^i_{\mathfrak m}(X)\) is equivalently \(\widehat{\operatorname{Ext}^{d-i}_R(X,\omega)}\).

For a field \(k\) and \(S=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_d]]\), the classes of inverse monomials \(x_1^{-a_1}\cdots x_d^{-a_d}\) with every \(a_j\ge1\) form a \(k\)-basis of \(H^d_{\mathfrak n}(S)\cong E_S(k)\). For \(d=0\) the empty monomial is the basis of \(k\).
For a field \(k\) and the noncomplete DVR \(T=k[t]_{(t)}\), \(H^1_{(t)}(T)\cong k(t)/T\) and its Matlis dual is \(k[[t]]\).

For a field \(k\) and \(R=k[[x,y]]/(x,y)^2\), \(\mathcal D_R\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_k(R,k)[0]\), with the \(R\)-action on the dual by precomposition with multiplication. The socle dimensions over \(k\) of \(R\) and of its dualizing module are two and one, respectively.
The Artinian local ring \(k[[x,y]]/(x,y)^2\) fails to be Gorenstein, as witnessed by its two-dimensional socle.

For any field \(k\), let \(R=k[[u,v]]/(uv)\) with maximal ideal \(\mathfrak m=(u,v)\). Then \(\omega_R\cong R\). For \(X=R\), \(H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R)=0\) and \(H^1_{\mathfrak m}(R)\cong E_R(k)\). For \(X=k\), \(H^0_{\mathfrak m}(k)\cong k\) and \(H^1_{\mathfrak m}(k)=0\).

The ring \(k[[u,v]]/(uv)\) identifies with pairs in \(k[[u]]\oplus k[[v]]\) with equal constant terms. In these coordinates the residue-field injective hull is the explicit quotient \((k((u))\oplus k((v)))/R\) via the indicated inclusion of \(R\).

For a field \(k\), \(S=k[[x,y]]\), and \(R=S/(x^2,xy)\) with maximal ideal \(\mathfrak m\), one has \(H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R)=kx\), \(H^1_{\mathfrak m}(R)\cong k((y))/k[[y]]\), \(H^{-1}(\mathcal D_R)\cong S/(x)\), and \(H^0(\mathcal D_R)\cong k\). All other cohomology of \(\mathcal D_R\) vanishes. The \(\mathcal D_R\) cohomology identifications are \(R\)-linear, using the quotient action on \(S/(x)\) and the residue-field action on \(k\).
Chapter orientation and literature pointers. Faithful flatness of Noetherian local completion is background used to motivate the study of formal fibres and valuation rings.

A ring is regular when all its prime localizations are regular local. A k-algebra T over a field k is geometrically regular when T ⊗ₖ k′ is Noetherian and regular for every finite field extension k′/k. A homomorphism of Noetherian rings A → B is regular when flat and its fibre B ⊗ₐ κ(𝔭) over every prime 𝔭 of A is geometrically regular over κ(𝔭). The formal fibre of a Noetherian local ring (A, 𝔪) at 𝔮 ∈ Spec A is Â ⊗ₐ κ(𝔮). A Noetherian ring R is a G-ring when the completion map of every prime localization R_𝔭 is regular. The J-2 condition on a Noetherian ring means that every finite-type algebra over it has open regular locus. A ring is catenary when all saturated prime chains between any given comparable pair of primes have the same length, and a Noetherian ring is universally catenary when all its finite-type algebras are catenary. A quasi-excellent ring is a Noetherian G-ring satisfying J-2. An excellent ring is a universally catenary quasi-excellent ring. The regular locus is the set of primes at which the local ring is regular local.
For every prime 𝔮 of a Noetherian local ring (A, 𝔪), its formal fibre Â ⊗ₐ κ(𝔮) identifies with widehat(A/𝔮) ⊗_{A/𝔮} Frac(A/𝔮), with completion on the right taken at 𝔪/𝔮.
For a flat local map A → B of Noetherian local rings, regularity of A and of the closed fibre B/𝔪_A B implies regularity of B. Conversely regularity of B implies regularity of A.

Polynomial rings in finitely many variables over a regular Noetherian ring, base changes T ⊗ₖ k′ of a regular Noetherian k-algebra T along a finite separable field extension k′/k, and maximal-ideal-adic completions of regular Noetherian local rings are regular.
Every ring derivation D:R → R extends to each localization of R and to the I-adic completion of R at any ideal I.
If R is Noetherian regular and D:R → R is a derivation with D(f) a unit for f ∈ R, then R[T]/(Tⁿ − f) is regular for every integer n ≥ 1.

For a field F of characteristic p > 0, Fᵖ is the subfield of p-th powers. A p-basis for F over a subfield containing Fᵖ is a family whose monomials of finite support with each exponent in {0,…,p−1} form a vector-space basis over that subfield. The subsequent characteristic-p results impose no finiteness bound on the imperfection degree of the coefficient field.

Let k be any field of characteristic p > 0, S = k[[u₁,…,uᵣ]][v₁,…,vₛ], and K = Frac S. There exists a family of subrings S_J of S such that S is finite free over each S_J and each contains Sᵖ. The fields K_J = Frac S_J are directed downward by inclusion. For every finite extension F/K, the intersection in F of the composita FᵖK_J is exactly Fᵖ.

For S and K as in X04, let B be a finite-type S-algebra which is a domain containing S, with fraction field F finite over K. For every f ∈ B outside Fᵖ, there exists a ring derivation D:B → B with D(f) ≠ 0.

Given a finite ring homomorphism A → B of Noetherian rings and 𝔭 ∈ Spec A, there is a canonical isomorphism widehat(A_𝔭) ⊗ₐ B ≅ ∏_{𝔭ᵢ∈Spec B, 𝔭ᵢ∩A=𝔭} widehat(B_{𝔭ᵢ}), using the respective maximal-ideal-adic completions and the empty product when no primes lie over 𝔭.
A finite algebra over a Noetherian G-ring and every localization of a Noetherian G-ring are G-rings.
Every Noetherian complete local ring and every finite-type algebra over any field or over ℤ are G-rings. Thus the completion map of every prime localization is regular in the sense of X01.
If R is a field, ℤ, or a Noetherian complete local ring, every finite-type R-algebra has open regular locus.
All Noetherian complete local rings, fields, ℤ, and finite-type algebras over a field or over ℤ are excellent.
Every localization of an excellent ring and every finite algebra over an excellent ring are excellent.
If A is a Noetherian local G-ring, its completion is normal when A is normal and is reduced when A is reduced, with these as two independent implications.

Regular maps of Noetherian rings are preserved by localization, by base change along finite-type maps, and by composition. For a pair A → B → C of maps of Noetherian rings, regularity of A → C and faithful flatness of B → C imply regularity of A → B.
Let A be a Noetherian complete local domain with fraction field K. For every prime 𝔓 of A[T], widehat(A[T]_𝔓) ⊗ₐ K is geometrically regular over K, with completion at the maximal ideal of A[T]_𝔓.
If A is Noetherian complete local, then A[T] is a G-ring.

Every essentially finite-type algebra over a Noetherian G-ring is a G-ring. Every essentially finite-type algebra over a quasi-excellent ring is quasi-excellent, and every essentially finite-type algebra over an excellent ring is excellent.

For a domain V with fraction field K, the following valuation-ring tests are equivalent and define a valuation ring: for every x ∈ K×, x or x⁻¹ belongs to V, the ideals of V are totally ordered by inclusion, and V is local with every finitely generated ideal principal.

Every local subring (A, 𝔪_A) of a field L is dominated by a valuation ring V of L (so Frac V = L): A ⊆ V and 𝔪_V ∩ A = 𝔪_A. If K ⊆ L is a subfield and A is a valuation ring of K, the dominating V satisfies V ∩ K = A.
For any domain A contained in a field L, its integral closure in L is the intersection in L of all valuation rings of L containing A.

For a valuation ring V of K, construct the totally ordered abelian group Γ = K×/V× with v(a) ≥ v(b) exactly when a/b ∈ V. In additive notation the quotient map obeys v(a+b) ≥ min(v(a),v(b)) whenever a,b,a+b are nonzero, with equality if the values differ. Conversely any homomorphism v from K× into a totally ordered abelian group satisfying this inequality defines a valuation ring {0} ∪ {x ∈ K× : v(x) ≥ 0} of K, whose value group identifies with the ordered image of v.

For a valuation ring V with fraction field K and value group Γ, the prime ideals P of V correspond in reverse inclusion order to the convex subgroups H of Γ. A subgroup is convex if it contains the order interval between any two of its elements. Under the correspondence, V_P has value group Γ/H with the quotient order, and V/P is a valuation ring of κ(P) = Frac(V/P) with value group H with its inherited order.

If U is a valuation ring and W is a valuation ring of its residue field, the inverse image V of W under U → κ(U) is a valuation ring of Frac U, implementing the composition of the valuations. The prime P = ker(U → κ(U)) considered in V has V/P ≅ W and V_P = U.
The rank of a valuation is the Krull dimension of its valuation ring. It equals the supremum of lengths of strict chains of convex subgroups in its value group.
A valuation ring is Noetherian if and only if it is a field or its value group is order-isomorphic to ℤ with the usual order. In the latter case it is a discrete valuation ring.

For any field k, assign to each nonzero f in k((x))((y)) the pair (ord_y(f), ord_x(leading y-coefficient of f)). This is a valuation with value group lexicographically ordered ℤ². Its only nonzero proper convex subgroup is 0 × ℤ. The associated coarsening is y-adic order and the residue valuation on k((x)) is x-adic order. The composed valuation ring has dimension two and is non-Noetherian.

For any field k the union of the fields k(t^{1/n!}), n ≥ 1, using the embedding sending the n-th generator to the (n+1)-st generator raised to n+1, has a compatible valuation given at stage n by order at its generator scaled by 1/n!. Its value group is ℚ, with no nonzero proper convex subgroup, so its valuation ring has dimension one and is non-Noetherian. This exhibits a rank-one valuation without discreteness.

Let V ⊆ W be valuation rings of fields K ⊆ L with W ∩ K = V. If L/K is finite, then [Γ_W:Γ_V] · [κ(W):κ(V)] ≤ [L:K], using the induced value-group inclusion and residue-field extension. Both factors are finite.

For a valuation ring V of K and any purely inseparable field extension L/K, including infinite extensions, V has a unique valuation-ring extension to L, and that extension is its integral closure in L.

For any prime p take k = 𝔽_p and choose f ∈ k[[t]] transcendental over k(t), which exists. Set K = k(t,fᵖ) and V = K ∩ k[[t]]. The restricted t-adic valuation has group ℤ, V is a DVR with uniformizer t, and V/tⁿV ≅ k[t]/(tⁿ) for n ≥ 1, giving V̂ ≅ k[[t]]. The generic formal fibre as a K-algebra is k((t)). The extension K(f)/K has degree p and base change to it gives k((t))[Z]/(Zᵖ − fᵖ) = k((t))[Z]/((Z−f)ᵖ), with the class of Z−f a nonzero nilpotent. Thus V is a DVR which fails the G-condition and hence is non-excellent. The DVR k[t]_{(t)} is excellent by X09.
Chapter roadmap and reference to the earlier linear lifting equation for lifting a map into a given ring.

For a square-zero surjection A' → A with kernel I, an A-algebra B, a B-module N, and an A-linear c:I→N, a lift is an A'-algebra surjection B'→B whose square-zero kernel is identified with N as a B-module and whose induced map on I is c. For a polynomial presentation P'=A'[X_i]→B with kernel Q, put Pbar=P'/IP', J=ker(Pbar→B), and K=im(IP'→Q/Q²).

With these hypotheses and presentation data, a lift exists exactly when the induced P'-linear map IP'→N factors through K and the resulting B-linear map K→N extends to Q/Q². After factorization, extension is equivalent to vanishing of its connecting class in Ext¹_B(J/J²,N) from 0→K→Q/Q²→J/J²→0. This test applies with any such polynomial presentation.

When the lifts of T01 exist, their isomorphism classes, with isomorphisms preserving B, N, and the A'-structure, form a torsor under the conormal cokernel T¹(B/A;N)=coker(Hom_B(Ω_{Pbar/A}⊗_{Pbar}B,N)→Hom_B(J/J²,N)), whose arrow is induced by the conormal differential.
For any chosen lift of T01, its A'-algebra automorphisms inducing the identity on B and N are naturally isomorphic as a group to the additive group Der_A(B,N), via d↦(z↦z+d(z mod N)).
The conormal cokernel T¹(B/A;N) identifies with derived Ext¹_B([J/J²→Ω_{Pbar/A}⊗_{Pbar}B],N), with the displayed conormal complex in cohomological degrees −1,0.

Take a square-zero surjection A'→A of local Artin k-algebras inducing identity on the specified residue field k, with kernel I, and a flat A-algebra B_A. A flat A'-algebra lifting B_A with its prescribed reduction gives a square-zero lift in the sense of T01 with N=I⊗_A B_A and c(i)=i⊗1. Conversely, a square-zero lift for these prescribed N,c is A'-flat and reduces to B_A.

A marked flat deformation of a k-algebra B over a local Artin k-algebra A with residue field k is a flat A-algebra B_A with a specified k-algebra isomorphism B_A⊗_A k≅B. An isomorphism of marked deformations is an A-algebra isomorphism commuting with the marking after reduction.

For a field k, a polynomial ring P=k[x₁,…,xₙ], a regular sequence f₁,…,fₛ in P, and B=P/(f₁,…,fₛ), every flat deformation of B over a local Artin k-algebra with specified residue field k lifts through any surjection of these algebras. The reduction of the lifted flat algebra along the surjection identifies with the given marked deformation.

Under the polynomial complete-intersection hypotheses of T04, the tangent space of isomorphism classes of marked flat deformations over k[ε]/(ε²), based at the trivial lift, is the cokernel of the B-linear Jacobian map Bⁿ→Bˢ sending (uⱼ) to (Σⱼ (∂fᵢ/∂xⱼ)uⱼ)ᵢ, with coefficients mapped to B.

For B=k[x]/(xᵐ), any field k and m≥1, the tangent space is B/(m x^{m−1}). Every marked first-order class is given by the equation xᵐ+εq(x) over k[ε]/(ε²), and two q have the same class precisely when their difference maps to zero in that quotient, also when char(k) divides m.

For a field k, take B=k⊕kx⊕ky⊕kz with the span of x,y,z square-zero. The free k[t]/(t²)-module on the marked basis 1,x,y,z becomes a commutative unital algebra by xy=tz, z²=ty and all other unordered products from x,y,z zero. It is a flat first-order deformation of B and admits no flat lift to k[t]/(t³).

The category A_k consists of local Artin k-algebras with specified residue field k and local k-algebra maps. A small extension is a surjection B→A whose kernel I has k-dimension one and is killed by the maximal ideal of B.
Every surjection in A_k is a finite composite of small extensions, up to identifying the last quotient with the target. An isomorphism needs no small-extension steps.

For a covariant F:A_k→Sets with F(k) a singleton use the canonical map F(A₁×_A A₂)→F(A₁)×_{F(A)}F(A₂). H1 requires surjectivity whenever A₂→A is small. H2 requires bijectivity for A=k and A₂=k[ε]/(ε²), for all A₁. H3 requires finite-dimensionality of the tangent space TF=F(k[ε]/(ε²)). H4 requires bijectivity for A₁=A₂ and both arrows the same small extension.

For a functor F as above satisfying H2, TF=F(k[ε]/(ε²)) acquires a natural k-vector space structure and for each finite-dimensional k-vector space I, viewed as a square-zero ideal in the split algebra k⊕I, there is a natural identification F(k⊕I)≃TF⊗_k I.

For F satisfying H2 and H1 in the split small-extension situation of T07, any prescribed compatible pair in F(A₁) and F(B) is represented, via the displayed fibre-product splitting and the canonical product identification, by the prescribed first component in F(A₁) and one tangent correction in TF⊗_k I.
If B→A is small with kernel I and h:A₁→B lifts the given A₁→A in A_k, there is an isomorphism A₁×_A B≅A₁×_k(k⊕I) sending (u,v) to (u, ū+(v−h(u))), where ū is the residue of u.

If F satisfies H1 and B→A is a surjection in A_k with kernel I annihilated by the maximal ideal of B, for every x∈F(A) there exists a least k-subspace J⊆I for which x lifts to F(B/J) via the induced quotient.

For a complete Noetherian local k-algebra R with residue field k, define h_R(A)=Hom_{k,loc}(R,A). A compatible family ξ_n∈F(R/m_Rⁿ) induces the natural map h_R→F by evaluating F on the factorization of each local map R→A through an Artin quotient R/m_Rⁿ.

A hull for F is a natural map h_R→F attached to a complete Noetherian local k-algebra with residue field k (and a compatible formal family), inducing an isomorphism on tangent spaces and such that h_R(B)→h_R(A)×_{F(A)}F(B) is surjective for each small extension B→A. Prorepresentability means a natural isomorphism with such an h_R on A_k.
For a functor F on A_k with F(k) a singleton, a hull exists if and only if H1, H2, and H3 hold.

Under H1–H3, the hull map h_R→F is a natural isomorphism on A_k precisely when H4 holds. Every functor prorepresented by a complete Noetherian local k-algebra with residue field k satisfies all four conditions H1–H4.

Recapitulation of the chapter's concrete conormal, ambiguity and flatness tests, and literature discussion of derived cotangent-complex obstructions in degree two, ambiguity in degree one and automorphisms in degree zero. The full construction and comparison are referred to external literature.
Motivation and proof roadmap for the alternating Tor length, diagonal reduction and its sign.

Module-length notation ℓ_R and grading and differential conventions: complexes are homologically graded except the indicated cohomological Čech complex, and the total differential on P_i⊗Q_j is d_P⊗1+(-1)^i 1⊗d_Q.
For a regular local ring (R,m) of dimension d and finite R-modules M,N with finite-length M⊗_R N, define the integer χ_R(M,N)=Σ_{i=0}^d (−1)^i ℓ_R Tor_i^R(M,N).
For the isolated intersection in I01, all Tor_i^R(M,N) have finite length, Tor_i^R(M,N)=0 for i>d, and χ_R(M,N)=χ_R(N,M).

In a regular local ring, for fixed finite N, χ_R(-,N) is additive on each short exact sequence of finite modules whose supports intersect Supp(N) only at most at the closed point. It is also additive in the other argument under the symmetric condition.

For finite M,N with isolated intersection in a regular local ring, they both admit finite prime filtrations. Using any such filtrations with respective factors R/p_a and R/q_b, all pairs of factors have isolated intersection and χ_R(M,N)=Σ_{a,b}χ_R(R/p_a,R/q_b). For each nonzero module, the maximum of the dimensions of its own filtration factors equals its dimension.

For closed supports X,Y in the spectrum of a regular local ring with intersection contained in the closed point, χ_R induces an integer-valued bilinear pairing on the Grothendieck groups of finite modules supported in X and Y, with relations from short exact sequences.

For a regular local ring R and finite modules M,N with finite-length tensor product, their maximal-ideal completions over the regular local completion Rhat again have finite-length tensor product and χ_Rhat(Mhat,Nhat)=χ_R(M,N). Completion preserves the dimension of R and the dimensions of its nonzero finite modules.

For a Noetherian local ring (A,n), finite E≠0 and an ideal J⊆n with finite-length E/JE, let P_{J,E}(t) be the eventual polynomial for ℓ_A(E/J^{t+1}E) at nonnegative integer t, of degree dim_A E and with positive leading coefficient. For integer r≥dim_A E define e_J^{(r)}(E)=r![t^r]P_{J,E}(t); this equals Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity at r=dim_A E and is zero for r>dim_A E. Put e_J^{(r)}(0)=0.

For finite E over a Noetherian local ring (A,n), let z=(z₁,…,zᵣ) generate J⊆n with E/JE of finite length. Every homology module of K_•(z;E) has finite length, and dim_A E≤r for E≠0. The equality Σ_{i=0}^r (−1)^i ℓ_A H_i(K_•(z;E))=e_J^{(r)}(E) holds, with a positive integer value if dim_A E=r and E≠0. This includes r=0 and the zero module with the stated zero convention.
For fixed J⊆n with r specified generators in the setting of I05, the degree-r formula e_J^{(r)} is additive on short exact sequences of finite modules with finite-length quotients by J.

For an R-regular sequence z of length r in the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring R and a nonzero finite N with N/(z)N of finite length, the alternating Tor length of (R/(z),N) through degree r equals e_{(z)}^{(r)}(N). It is zero for dim_R N<r and positive for dim_R N=r.

In I06, if R is regular local of dimension d, then dim_R R/(z)=d−r. Thus for this complete-intersection factor the isolated-intersection Euler characteristic vanishes when the sum of dimensions is less than d and is positive when the sum is d, in any characteristic.

For a field k, let A=k[[x₁,…,xₐ]], B=k[[y₁,…,y_b]], S=k[[x₁,…,xₐ,y₁,…,y_b]]. For finite modules M over A and N over B, the completed exterior tensor product is the natural finite S-module M⊠_k N=(S⊗_A M)⊗_B N. It is separately exact on finite modules and is naturally isomorphic to lim←_{u,v}(M/(x)^u M)⊗_k(N/(y)^v N) via the truncation transition maps.
For nonzero finite M,N over the respective power-series rings of I07 and s=(x,y)S, dim_S(M⊠_k N)=dim_A M+dim_B N and e_s(M⊠_k N)=e_{(x)}(M)e_{(y)}(N).

For a field k and R=k[[x₁,…,x_d]], let M,N be nonzero finite R-modules with finite-length tensor product. Regard N as a module over the y-copy, form T=M⊠_k N over S=k[[x,y]] and let J=(x₁−y₁,…,x_d−y_d). For every i, Tor_i^R(M,N)≅H_i(K_•(x−y;T)) over R≅S/J, and χ_R(M,N)=e_J^{(d)}(T).

In every equal-characteristic regular local ring of dimension d, if M,N are nonzero finite modules with finite-length tensor product then dim_R M+dim_R N≤d. The Tor Euler characteristic is zero if the inequality is strict and positive if it is equality.

Let S be Noetherian local, h a nonzero divisor in its maximal ideal, and A=S/(h). For finite A-modules M,N with M⊗_A N of finite length, assume M admits a finite free A-resolution and N a finite free S-resolution. Then the finite alternating sum of the S-lengths of Tor_i^S(M,N) is zero.

Let V be a complete DVR with uniformizer π and residue field k, R=V[[x₁,…,xₐ]], S=V[[x₁,…,xₐ,y₁,…,yₐ]]. For nonzero finite R-modules M,N on which π is injective, put T=(S⊗_{V[[x]]}M)⊗_{V[[y]]}N using N over the y-copy. Multiplication by π is injective on T, T/πT≅(M/πM)⊠_k(N/πN), and dim_S T=dim_R M+dim_R N−1.
Under the DVR and module hypotheses of I11, for J=(x₁−y₁,…,xₐ−yₐ) the diagonal Koszul complex K_•(x−y;T) computes Tor_i^R(M,N) in every degree, with R≅S/J.

For a regular local ring (R,m) of dimension d and mixed characteristic (0,p) with p∉m², and nonzero finite R-modules M,N meeting only at the closed point, dim_R M+dim_R N≤d. The value χ_R(M,N) is zero in the strict-inequality case and positive in the equality case.
For any regular local ring R of dimension d, in any characteristic, nonzero finite R-modules M,N with finite-length tensor product satisfy dim_R M+dim_R N≤d.
For a regular local ring R and prime ideals p,q of R, if a prime ideal r is minimal over p+q then ht(r)≤ht(p)+ht(q).

Let (A,n) be Noetherian local, F_• a finite free complex in homological degrees 0,…,s, and U a nonzero finite A-module. If all homology of F_•⊗_A U has finite length and some is nonzero, then s≥depth_A U. In particular, a nonexact finite free complex with finite-length homology over a Cohen–Macaulay local ring has length at least the dimension of the ring.

For nonzero finite modules M,N over a Noetherian local ring R with finite-length M⊗_R N and finite pd_R M, depth_R N≤pd_R M. Also dim_R N≤pd_R M if N is Cohen–Macaulay, and the same dimension inequality holds for arbitrary such N if R is regular local.
For a field k and each integer b≥1 in R=k[[x,y]], χ_R(R/(y),R/(y−xᵇ))=b. The two axes have χ_R(R/(x),R/(y))=1.

For R=k[[x,y,z]] over a field k, R/(x,y) and R/(y,z) meet only at the closed point. Their tensor product has length one, but their Tor Euler characteristic is zero. The Tor modules in degrees 0 and 1 each identify with the residue field k, and the higher Tor modules vanish.

For bounded complexes F_•,G_• of finite free modules over a Noetherian local ring, suppose their unions of homology supports intersect at most at the closed point. The homology of the total tensor complex has finite length, so its alternating length defines a pairing additive separately on degreewise short exact sequences of eligible bounded free complexes. In either variable a homology isomorphism between such complexes preserves the pairing.

The supported Euler pairing of I17 gives χ_R(M,N) when evaluated on finite free resolutions of the modules of I01. The same expression is defined on perfect complexes represented by bounded finite free complexes with isolated intersection of homological supports and is independent of the choices of such representatives.

Appendix A explains the separate roles of the regular quotient cover for local duality and the finite regular subring for nonvanishing, and cites the input formal lifting, split conormal and completion results.
Every field L is formally smooth over its prime field, without a finite generation assumption.
For a flat ring map A→B and an ideal K of A with K²=0, if B/KB is formally smooth over A/K then B is formally smooth over A.

For every field k of positive characteristic p there exists a complete discrete valuation ring Λ with uniformizer the integer p and residue field k, such that for every n≥1 the map ℤ/p^n → Λ/p^nΛ is formally smooth. The same Λ works for all n.
For every complete Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪,k) of equal characteristic, a coefficient field map k→R exists that induces the identity on the residue field k.

For any complete Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪,k) with residue field of characteristic p>0, there is a continuous map Λ→R from a coefficient DVR as in C02, inducing the identity on k. Its kernel is zero if p is not nilpotent in R, and is (p^e) when e is least with p^e=0 in R.
Every complete Noetherian local ring R is the quotient of a complete regular local ring S by a local surjection inducing the identity on their common residue field.
Every complete regular local ring (R,𝔪,k) of equal characteristic and dimension d is isomorphic to k[[X_1,…,X_d]], with coefficient field and the given residue field.

A complete regular local ring (R,𝔪,k) of dimension d and mixed characteristic (0,p) with p∉𝔪² is isomorphic to Λ[[X_1,…,X_{d−1}]], for a complete coefficient DVR Λ of the kind in C02, with uniformizer p and residue field k.

Every complete Noetherian local domain (B,𝔪,k) of dimension d contains a complete regular local subring (S,𝔫,k) of dimension d whose inclusion induces the identity on the common residue field k, such that B is a finite S-module and √(𝔫B)=𝔪.
Bibliographic apparatus and citations to prerequisites and literature. These citations do not add formalization obligations to this volume.
For a cochain complex U over a Noetherian local ring and the residue injective hull E, there is a natural isomorphism H^j(Hom(U,E[0])) ≅ Hom(H^{-j}(U),E).
For any R-complex U and the coinduced dualizing model of the complete regular local cover S→R, RHom_R(U,𝒟_R) ≅ RHom_S(U,S[n]), with the R-action on the right by precomposition.

The explicitly allocated ramified presentation in the proof of I13: a complete mixed-characteristic regular local ring R of dimension d with p in the square of its maximal ideal is a quotient of the unramified ring S=V[[X₁,…,X_d]] by h=p−f, with V a coefficient DVR of uniformizer p and the same residue field, f in the square of the variable ideal, and h a regular element outside the square of the maximal ideal of S.
For finite modules the tensor support is the intersection of the supports. Over the Noetherian local base a finite module has finite length exactly when its support is contained in the closed point.
Changing the degree-n identification with the chosen residue-field injective hull postcomposes the derived torsion comparison by the corresponding shifted hull automorphism.

The finite regular normalization of a complete local domain can be chosen as a power series ring over the coefficient field in equal characteristic or over a complete p-DVR in mixed characteristic, mapping its variables to parameters of B or to lifts of parameters of B/pB, respectively.

The finite regular normalization can be chosen from series on a system of parameters over the coefficient field, or on lifts of a parameter system modulo p over the coefficient DVR, according to characteristic.
